LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup, plus a preview and prediction Patrick Smith/Getty Images In the Week 10 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the New York Giants play host to the division rival Washington Commanders . New York enters this game riding high atop the NFC East, having won each of its last two games sandwiching a Week 8 bye. The Giants are surprisingly in the playoff picture in the first year of the John Harbaugh era despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart in Week 2. They recently turned to J.J. McCarthy in place of Jameis Winston but kept on winning. Washington climbed out of last place in the NFC East thanks to a Week 8 win over the lowly Philadelphia Eagles but still has the second-worst record in the conference. The Commanders missed an opportunity for a win the last time these two teams played by mismanaging the clock as poorly as any team ever has, and they will surely be looking to atone for that mistake here. Will the Giants keep rolling, or will the Commanders capture a rare victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Giants vs. Commanders live Date: Thursday, Nov. 12 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford, New Jersey) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Giants -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Commanders have the ball The Commanders are not particularly effective either passing or running the football. They rank 21st in the NFL in net yards per pass attempt (which accounts for yards lost to sacks), and they're 23rd in designed rushing yards per carry, which eliminates scrambling from the picture. Their most effective form of offense is scrambling, where Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota have run 29 times for 274 yards — the most scramble yards in the NFL, per Tru Media. But that's not something that you can lean on down-to-down. Daniels has completed only 63.9% of his passes at an average of 6.9 yards per attempt. While he has seven passing touchdowns and has yet to be intercepted, he has a low passing success rate (43.9%, according to Tru Media), has generated explosives at only an average rate (7.8%) and has struggled on third downs (30.9%). Again, his most effective way of moving the ball has been via the scramble. The Giants are actually second in the NFL in passing success rate allowed and third in explosives per dropback, according to Tru Media. So Daniels, with his limited receiving corps in the absence of Terry McLaurin , might find it difficult to move the ball through the air. The Giants, though, have been vulnerable to opponent scrambles, allowing quarterbacks to take off downfield on a league-high 23.9% of pressured dropbacks and yielding 225 scramble yards to date. So Daniels could have some room to run. In the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt , the Commies have turned to Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler in the backfield. They have not been particularly effective on the ground, but they're each capable outlet receivers for Daniels, who has targeted backs on 14.4% of his passes, a slightly higher rate than last year (12.8%). Doing so against the Giants may not be the most advisable strategy, though, because it means testing rookie linebacker Arvell Reese in space, and Reese has been a space-eating demon so far this season. Daniels' other pass-catchers at the moment are Stefon Diggs , Antonio Williams , Van Jefferson and Chig Okonkwo. The Giants have been good at limiting tight ends over the middle (there's Reese showing up again), so the passing game might run through the perimeter receivers, who will face off with an improved Deonte Banks and the recently-extended Greg Newsome II on the outside. Look for Daniels to at least try to test those guys deep down the field, given he has the seventh-highest deep throw rate among qualified quarterbacks. The Giants have faced deep passes at essentially an average rate so far this season, and they've been excellent at defending them, checking in second in EPA per dropback on those plays. Still, dinking and dunking hasn't been all that effective for Daniels and the Commanders, so they're going to have to try to hit on a few big plays. When the Giants have the ball The Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy as their quarterback in garbage time of their loss to the Saints back in Week 6, and they have stuck with him over the last two games. They've been a somewhat unusual offense with McCarthy under center. McCarthy himself has not been efficient on a down-to-down basis. He's completed only 63.2% of his passes, and he has one touchdown pass and one interception. He checks in 31st in success rate among 37 quarterbacks with at least 75 dropbacks this season, according to Tru Media. But McCarthy is averaging 9.1 (!!!!) yards per attempt, and he's 15th among the same group of 37 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's because when he does complete passes, they're basically all going for big gains in big situations. He's throwing the ball farther downfield than anyone in the league (10.6-yard average depth of target), and he's leading the NFL in explosive plays per dropback at 16.0%, per Tru Media. The Commanders' defense is essentially the opposite of what McCarthy has done so far. They yield a high passing success rate (21st in the league) but a low explosive rate (11th). The tension between those two poles will be interesting to watch play out on Monday night. When McCarthy drops back to pass, he is looking most often to Malik Nabers , who has been the intended receiver on 31.7% of McCarthy's throws. Malachi Fields , not Isaiah Likely , has been the secondary target, with a 20.6% target share compared to Likely's 17.5% rate. Before McCarthy took over at quarterback, Likely tied Nabers for the team lead in target share at 29.4%, compared to just 11.2% for Fields. Nabers and Fields will do most of their work against Rasul Douglas and Amik Robertson on the outside, while Likely will see a lot of rookie linebacker Sonny Styles , slot corner Mike Sainristil and safeties Jeremy Reaves and Nick Cross . The Commanders have not generated very much pressure this season (33.5% of opponent dropbacks, per Tru Media, 25th in the league), while McCarthy has been one of the league's most-pressured quarterbacks since taking over. He tends to hold the ball for a while as he looks to push it down the field. Whether the Commanders can get after him will go a long way toward determining whether he can complete any big plays. Cam Skattebo is back for the Giants in this game, and he's likely to take over the lead role from Devin Singletary , who struggled last week and is more suited to being a passing-down back. Skattebo hasn't been very effective as a rusher this season, averaging 4.3 yards per carry with a 45.9% success rate, but he had his best game of the year before sitting out last week after the bye. The Commanders have been solid against the run, yielding only 3.9 yards per carry, with below-average marks both before (1.09) and after contact (2.83). This might be a game where the Giants lean on those big plays from McCarthy. I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run? This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Commanders +2.5): The last time these two teams faced off, they TIED. I'm expecting another close game and may be leaning toward the underdog. Washington played the Los Angeles Rams tough last Sunday and held Matthew Stafford and Co. to 20 points. J.J. McCarthy has looked solid with his new team, but he actually just became the only quarterback in the past 40 seasons to register a win with zero passing touchdowns in four straight starts (dating back to last year). He suffered a hip injury vs. the Philadelphia Eagles , while Cam Skattebo is coming off a hamstring strain. Both will play, but I do wonder how much those issues could linger. The Commanders are 4-0-1 straight up and 4-1 against the spread (ATS) in their last five against the New York Giants , so I'll take the points here in a potential upset. … Prediction: Commanders 21, Giants 20 Dubin (Giants -2.5): I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith that this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. … Prediction: Giants 20, Commanders 14 New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions (-2.5) (Munich) Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20 Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late. … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21 Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17 Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game. … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14 San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) at Dallas Cowboys Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26 Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. The Niners are so efficient on a per-play basis both on the ground and through the air, and the Cowboys make even bad offenses look competent. Dallas might be able to get something going on its side of the ball, especially if George Pickens returns to the lineup, but I don't expect it to be nearly enough to compete with what San Francisco does on offense. … Prediction: 49ers 34, Cowboys 23 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) (SNF) Dajani (Bengals -3.5): I'll keep saying it, this may be Joe Burrow 's year to win MVP. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. The Bengals have scored 34 points in three straight games and 30 points in four straight games. The Steelers defeated the Bengals in Pittsburgh in Week 3, 30-27, but the Bengals will even the series on Sunday night. Cincy is 7-2 SU and ATS in its last nine home primetime games. … Prediction: Bengals 30, Steelers 24 Dubin (Steelers +3.5): I'm taking the Bengals to win, but I like the Steelers to keep things uncomfortably close. McCarthy and Cam Skattebo are tracking towards playing. The total remains a rather low one (41.5) after these teams combined for 54 points in a tie earlier this season. Commanders vs. Giants Score Prediction Earlier this week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite pick for every game in Week 10 in his Road to 272 column . He’s targeting New York as a home favorite to cover: I may have included the New York Giants in last week's edition of my Fraud Rankings , but my biggest issue with them has been their strength of schedule. Will I be betting on them when they take on teams like the Jaguars and 49ers in the coming weeks? Likely not, but they once again have a game against a bad team on Thursday Night Football when they face the Washington Commanders, and much like the majority of the season, I expect them to take care of business against an inferior opponent. These two teams played to a tie in Week 5 earlier this season, but with it being a road game for the Giants and the fact that they had Jameis Winston at quarterback, I think we can admit they're in a better spot in the rematch. J.J. McCarthy has been surprisingly solid to begin his tenure with the Giants, ranking fifth in the NFL in completion percentage over expected (+5.3%) amongst quarterbacks who have played 60+ snaps this season. It's also no coincidence that over the last three weeks, the Giants have led the league in net yards per play at +1.5. Meanwhile, the Commanders continue to be a poorly coached team that doesn't thrive in any area, ranking in the bottom half of the NFL in virtually every metric. The Giants may not be a Super Bowl contender because of their shaky quarterback situation, but it’s pretty clear that Harbaugh has put this team in position to make the playoffs. New York is No. 10 in EPA/Play on defense, No. 15 in EPA/Play on offense and has been one of the top teams in the league against the spread, covering in six of eight games. Daniels has played well in the 2026 season, but it hasn’t been enough with this offense ranking in the bottom 12 in the league in several key metrics and the defense clocking in at No. 19 in EPA/Play. At home, I’m taking the Giants to keep their winning ways going as they try to secure the top spot in the NFC East. away.blurb: Rams Injury Report, Week 9 at Commanders: Myles Garrett expected to play; Trent McDuffie, Colby Parkinson, and Kam Curl questionable; Terrance Ferguson ruled out Skip to main content Primary nav TEAM "We're still working through those types of things," McVay said Friday morning prior to practice, when asked what kind of ramp-up he expects in terms of how much Garrett is able to play on Sunday. "He's really done a great job in practice. He'll be a DNP today, but it's more of just being smart with him. Nothing to do with anything other than he has progressed really well, made a tremendous impact in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, feels really comfortable with the game plan, and it's been great having him out there, as well as (tight end) Terrance (Ferguson)." While Ferguson (ankle) also returned to practice this week, and was expected to play Sunday according to McVay, he ended up being ruled out after the Rams sent out an updated injury report. Initially listed on this week's report with an ankle injury, Ferguson picked up a hamstring injury in Friday's practice based on the injury updated report. Meanwhile, Trent McDuffie (back) and tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs) are listed as questionable for Sunday's game, as well as inside linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back) and safety Kam Curl (foot). Long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) is listed as doubtful, which would set up Jake McQuaide to be up from the practice squad again. McVay also said cornerback Jaylen Watson is listed as out, but will be placed on IR. Otherwise, all other Rams players listed on the injury report do not have a game status designation. For the Commanders, wide receivers Treylon Burks (foot) and Dyami Brown (calf) have been ruled out, while defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton (pectoral) is listed as questionable. home.blurb: Commanders-Giants Final Injury Report: Lucas Patrick Out, Treylon Burks Expected Back Despite Missed Practice Skip to main content SI.COM Lucas Patrick is out Thursday night against the New York Giants. The Commanders’ final injury report also ruled out tight end Colson Yankoff, leaving Washington to start Nick Allegretti at center in place of Patrick. Patrick entered concussion protocol during Sunday’s loss to the Rams, and rookie Matt Gulbin finished that game at center. Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed Tuesday that Allegretti will start against New York. Gulbin got the call Sunday because he had been taking the center reps while Allegretti worked at guard, a decision I wrote more about earlier this week . According to Washington's official website, the Giants blitz at the third-highest rate in the NFL. Allegretti will have to help set the protection against that defense with Jayden Daniels behind him. Treylon Burks missed Wednesday’s practice with the foot injury that kept him out against the Rams, but he has no game designation. Quinn said the day off was planned after Burks got work Tuesday and that the receiver was expected to be ready Thursday. Washington did not practice Monday and held a walkthrough Tuesday, so those first two participation reports were estimates. Burks’ place on the active list will be confirmed with Thursday’s inactives. Yankoff did not practice during the short week because of a knee injury. His absence reaches beyond the tight end rotation: Washington credited him with 185 special teams snaps this season. John Bates (shoulder) was full all three days, and Chig Okonkwo (hip) was full Tuesday and Wednesday. Neither has a game designation. home.blurb: Washington has ruled out center Lucas Patrick and tight end Colson Yankoff, while Giants linebacker Malik Harrison is questionable with a groin injury. Patrick has been ruled out after suffering a concussion during Washington's Week 9 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. He did not practice throughout the short week, and head coach Dan Quinn confirmed that Nick Allegretti will start at center against New York. Yankoff will miss Thursday's game after being held out of all three practices. The tight end has been dealing with a knee injury since last week and is also a contributor on special teams. Burks did not practice Wednesday but carries no game status designation. After missing the Week 9 matchup against the Rams, Quinn indicated that the receiver should be available Thursday. Robertson was limited Wednesday after practicing fully earlier in the week but carries no game status designation. Harrison is the only Giants player listed as questionable for Thursday's matchup. New York has no players ruled out or listed as doubtful. Skattebo carries no injury designation after missing Sunday's victory over the Philadelphia Eagles. The running back returned to full practice participation Tuesday, and head coach John Harbaugh indicated he expects Skattebo to be available Thursday. picks.blurb: Odds Detroit Lions Beat New England Patriots in Week 10 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Detroit Lions travel overseas to take on the reigning AFC champion New England Patriots in Munich, Germany, on Sunday morning (9:30 a.m. EST). The Patriots, which are off to a 5-4 start, are coming off a 45-27 defeat at the hands of Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers. Meanwhile, the Lions, which are sitting at 6-2, defeated the Miami Dolphins, 19-9, in their Week 9 tilt . New England – led by Mike Vrabel on the sidelines – has lost two of its last three games, including to the Chicago Bears in Week 7. Additionally, it sits basically in the middle of the pack in both points scored (23.4/game) and points allowed (23.0/g). Yet, the Patriots still possess a myriad of talent on both sides of the ball. On offense, they're led under center by third-year passer Drake Maye, who has thrown for 18 touchdowns, 2,282 yards and a league-high 11 interceptions through nine games. He's coming off a three-interception performance against the Packers in which he completed a season-low 55.3 percent of his passes. Maye's top target this year has been veteran tight end Hunter Henry, who has amassed 32 catches, 361 yards and two touchdowns through the season's first nine games. And on the ground, the Patriots are spearheaded by sixth-year back Rhamondre Stevenson. Stevenson, a fourth-round pick of New England, has accumulated 399 yards and two touchdowns, and is presently averaging 3.9 yards per carry. Then, on the defensive side of the ball, the Patriots have received strong performances this season from the likes of EDGE defenders Gabe Jacas and Elijah Ponder, cornerback Carlton Davis III and linebacker Christian Elliss. Ponder, a second-year pro , has already recorded 7.5 sacks, eight tackles for loss and 13 QB hits, and has returned a fumble for a touchdown. And for his efforts, he's earned a 75.0 overall grade from Pro Football Focus, the 23rd-best overall grade among 110 qualified players at the position. The Patriots will not, however, have the services of Davis (knee) for this Week 10 international affair. Plus, they will also be down starting left guard Ben Brown (knee), and are expected to be without Stevenson (knee). Stevenson, the team's No. 1 back, suffered a plantaris tendon tear last week against the Packers. Those are three significant losses for Vrabel's squad going into its matchup with Detroit. As for the Lions, they will also be down multiple starters in Week 10: linebacker Jack Campbell (neck), center Cade Mays (ankle) and cornerback D.J. Reed (hip). Plus, safety Kerby Joseph, who has yet to play a single game in 2026, will not be making his season debut in Germany. While both teams are rather significantly banged up, I still believe this matchup favors Detroit. At this present juncture, I believe the Lions have a 59 percent chance to secure their fifth straight victory. It's been 11 seasons since the Lions last played an international game, but this trip has been in the works for some time. In 2024, as part of the NFL's Global Markets Program, the Lions have had marketing rights in the DACH region , which includes Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Since then, the team has made several trips to Germany and has helped support Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown— whose mother, Miriam Brown, was born and raised in Germany —in running youth football programs across the country. As for the game itself, it looks like it'll be a good one, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -2.5 points . While the Lions are riding a four-game winning streak, the Patriots' 2026 season has been a more up-and-down affair after reaching the Super Bowl in 2025. They opened the season by losing to the Seahawks, beat the Steelers, then lost to the Jaguars over the first three weeks. They got back to 2-2 with a big win over the Bills, then rallied to 4-2 after wins over the Raiders and Jets. The Bears took them down on Thursday night in Week 7, but the Patriots eeked out a five-point win over the Dolphins to reach 5-3. On Sunday, the Patriots took on the Packers and looked completely unprepared. Packer QB Jordan Love jumped all over them, throwing for 372 yards and three scores, while Patriots Drake Maye threw for 299 yards and three scores, but also threw three interceptions and was sacked four times. On the ground, the Packers' worst-ranked rushing offense ran for 129 yards and two touchdowns, while the Pats gained 94 rushing yards, a touchdown, and lost a fumble. In the end, the Packers left Foxborough with a 45-27 win, and left former Patriots QB and current color commentator Tom Brady wondering who this New England team actually is: "Half the season they played like this, and the other half of the season they haven't turned the ball over, they haven't exposed the defense, have played more physical on defense, but right now it's just too inconsistent. Which team are they going to get? The team that is loose with the ball, is loose with decision-making, looking like they can be beaten by anybody. Or the team that takes care of the football, that makes the other team play left-handed, and can do what they want to do. Can they be a good team? They haven't quite done that because good teams leave the smallest margin of error." The Lions and Patriots are scheduled to play on Sunday, November 15, at 9:30 a.m. ET at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.

Injuries and inconsistencies are a big reason for that, but so is the drop-off in play from Drake Maye. He has already set a career-high in interceptions with 11, giving New England fans a legitimate reason to be concerned. away.blurb: Patriots QB Drake Maye Calls Out Media Over Reports About Injured Teammate - Newsweek U.S. News Patriots QB Drake Maye Calls Out Media Over Reports About Injured Teammate Published Surprisingly, previous reports indicated Stevenson would miss weeks due to an injury. However, the running back's recent appearance at practice raises the possibility of an earlier return, which could provide a major boost when the team faces the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany, this weekend. During a press conference on Thursday, Maye addressed those previous reports about his teammate, calling out the media over the accuracy of its information. "I think that just speaks to, first off, the media not really knowing 100% what they’re talking about a lot of the time… [He’s] a guy that wants to be out there. Wants to be back for his team. … We’re in the midst of planning to make a run here and win a big one before the bye. So, this is a time for a lot of the players on this team to try and get out there, play with their teammates. [I know] that he’s a great player and he can help us out," Maye told reporters . Earlier this week, ESPN's Mike Reiss cited NFL insider Ian Rapoport, who reported that Stevenson was dealing with an injury to the back of his knee, and it was "expected to keep him out the next few weeks." ESPN's Reiss shared a video on Thursday showing Stevenson participating in drills off to the side after the team landed in Munich. As of this writing, he's still listed as "doubtful" on the team's injury report for Sunday's game. With the Patriots looking to bounce back from last weekend's loss to the Green Bay Packers, they can use all the help they can get. Wide receiver AJ Brown participated in Thursday's "jog-through" with the team, giving positive signs about his potential return from knee and ankle injuries. But running back TreVeyon Henderson, offensive lineman Ben Brown and cornerback Carlton Davis III stayed among the sidelined in Foxborough and have officially been ruled out for the matchup in Munich. RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness — out) CB Carlton Davis III (knee — out) An illness that kept Henderson hospitalized for multiple days will now keep the running back out for a third straight game. And in the secondary, a knee injury will also keep Davis from taking the field in Munich after he’d worked back from a neck injury throughout October. That leaves four non-participants from Wednesday potentially in play for the NFL international series. The reigning AFC Offensive Player of the Month completed 55 percent of his passes for 299 yards with three touchdowns and three interceptions last weekend. home.headline: A big Munich test for Lions and Patriots as injuries loom for New England
home.blurb: Injuries are a top concern for New England. Before traveling Wednesday night, the Patriots ruled out LG Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness). November 12, 2026 / 5:07 PM EST / AP Heading into international games, NFL coaches typically talk up the niceties of "growing the game" globally. The New England Patriots (5-4) have lost two of their past three games and have a slew of injury concerns, including running back Rhamondre Stevenson. The Detroit Lions, even with a 6-2 record and four straight victories, are trying to keep pace in the tight NFC North. Sunday's game in Munich is a big one for both teams. Lions coach Dan Campbell wasn't focused on the international implications. "Well, if I'm being honest, I just haven't thought that far into it. I'm like, 'We've got to get prepared,'" Campbell said. The Patriots were embarrassed at home by the Green Bay Packers last week, losing 45-27, with Drake Maye throwing three interceptions and the secondary struggling to contain the Packers' passing game. Campbell expects a much-improved New England team on Sunday. "You look at the totality of what this team is capable of, the firepower they have, and they're a good team. They're dangerous," he said. "And they're going to clean a lot of things up." The Lions slogged through a 19-9 win over the rebuilding Miami Dolphins last week, relying on four field goals from Jake Bates. It was also just one week after a neck injury to All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell. Detroit's bye week is in the rearview mirror, and after Munich, the team will host Tampa Bay and then Chicago on Thanksgiving Day. "It's a good thing to be tested during the season," Campbell said. "It really is. And to have to go through some of these tough stretches because that's what the playoffs are. That's what it is. And certainly if you got to go on the road. So, that's what this is. This is about us. This is the next obstacle we have. Told the team we're not going to clear it. Our objective is to go through it, and that's the mindset." Stevenson, the team's leading rusher with 399 yards on 102 carries, didn't practice Wednesday because of a knee injury. That could put second-year running back Corey Kiner in line for the bulk of the carries. "Corey has done a really nice job, but there are also some things that Corey has to be able to improve on," coach Mike Vrabel said, citing "recognition of the pressure and then the ability to block the pressure." The coach said "a lot of contending teams" are 5-4. "We've got to start putting ourselves in position to play meaningful games in January or in the middle of January," Vrabel said. "It's usually what happens in the National Football League; a bunch of teams get bunched up, and they go in different directions, and I know the direction that we're going to head in, and that's going to be the one that's forward, positive and winning." home.blurb: Wide receiver A.J. Brown was on hand for it. After missing back-to-back weeks due to a knee issue in addition to the high ankle sprain that sent him to injured reserve in September, the former All-Pro returned as a limited participant to begin Detroit Lions prep. But running back TreVeyon Henderson, offensive lineman Ben Brown and cornerback Carlton Davis III stayed among the sidelined in Foxborough and have officially been ruled out for the matchup in Munich. RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness — out) CB Carlton Davis III (knee — out) An illness that kept Henderson hospitalized for multiple days will now keep the running back out for a third straight game. The Patriots will be without another Brown on offense after the team’s starting left guard exited last Sunday’s 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers with a knee injury. And in the secondary, a knee injury will also keep Davis from taking the field in Munich after he’d worked back from a neck injury throughout October. That leaves four non-participants from Wednesday potentially in play for the NFL international series. FB Reggie Gilliam (knee — IR return) G Greg Van Roten (hamstring — IR return) S Kerby Joseph (knee — PUP return) But a pair of 21-day practice windows are now open for New England along with one 53-man roster spot. After Van Roten headed back to practice last week, Gilliam did so to start work on the Lions. The fullback spent the past five games on injured reserve. Kansas City got back into the win column Sunday at Arrowhead Stadium after consecutive losses to the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos . The victory helped the Chiefs regain some momentum as they continue their pursuit of the AFC West title and the conference's top playoff seed. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , Kansas City opened as a 3.5-point road favorite against Atlanta. The game's opening over/under is set at 46.5 points. The Falcons enter the matchup looking to turn their season around after a difficult first half. Despite offensive weapons like running back Bijan Robinson and wide receiver Drake London, Atlanta has struggled to turn its talent into consistent wins. On defense, the Falcons will be down starting safety Jessie Bates, who has a track record of intercepting quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Bates is being traded to the Jacksonville Jaguars . For Kansas City, the matchup presents another opportunity to build momentum after Sunday's win. The Chiefs' defense rediscovered its pass rush against the Jets, while the offense will look to be more consistent heading into the second half of the season. Although Kansas City enters as the favorite, the relatively narrow spread suggests oddsmakers expect a competitive road contest.

They are each within one half-game of first place in their respective divisions. The Broncos lead Kansas City in the AFC West while the Falcons are looking up at the Panthers and the Saints in the NFC South. This despite Atlanta having lost two in a row and the Chiefs two of their last three. Kansas City is coming off a convincing 35-12 win over the New York Jets, a game that turned after the Chiefs trailed 12-7 in the second quarter. Patrick Mahomes completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns, both scoring passes going to Kenneth Walker III , who was the offensive centerpiece with 102 rushing yards, 143 yards from scrimmage and three total touchdowns. Travis Kelce added 72 receiving yards and even scored on a one-yard run. The defense took over after halftime, holding New York scoreless in the final thirty minutes as the Chiefs pulled away with 21 unanswered second-half points. Kansas City also went 4-for-4 in the red zone, an encouraging development after back-to-back losses to Seattle and Denver. Mahomes did briefly leave the field after hurting his arm/elbow on a strip-sack but returned and finished the game. As a result, the injury report is worth following as gametime approaches. Atlanta, meanwhile, returns home after a disappointing 34-17 loss to Cincinnati in Madrid, its second straight defeat following a 16-0 shutout loss at Tampa Bay. The Falcons opened strongly against the Bengals with an 80-yard drive resulting in a Michael Penix Jr. touchdown pass to Charlie Woerner . The scoring continued as they took a 10-7 lead later in the first quarter, but Cincinnati answered with 17 unanswered points in the second quarter and Atlanta never recovered. Penix finished 20-of-31 for 162 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Bijan Robinson supplied the offense’s biggest bright spot with 100 rushing yards and a touchdown on 19 carries. Drake London caught five passes for 68 yards, but Atlanta committed 12 penalties for 88 yards and allowed Joe Burrow to throw three touchdown passes. The central storyline from Atlanta’s perspective is will they be able to control the ball and keep Mahomes and co. off the field? The Falcons average 138.8 yards rushing per game. For Kansas City, it is about limiting Bijan Robinson and Atlanta’s rushing attack. The Chiefs have thrived against the run to date this season allowing just 96.3 yards on the ground per game. These teams last met two seasons ago. Mercedes-Benz Stadium was the site and Kansas City won 22-17. Mahomes threw for 217 yards and two touchdowns, while Rashee Rice caught 12 passes for 110 yards and a score; Atlanta, then quarterbacked by Kirk Cousins , had a chance late but could not complete the comeback. picks.headline: Chiefs-Falcons betting line & prediction: Will Josh Downs make instant impact?
picks.blurb: Read our AI Policy. The Chiefs acquired receiver Josh Downs, who is expected to debut Sunday in Atlanta. Patrick Mahomes practiced fully Wednesday after an elbow injury scare vs. Jets. The betting line lists Kansas City as a 3.5-point favorite over Atlanta. The Kansas City Chiefs stopped a two-game losing streak Sunday with their 35-12 win over the New York Jets to improve to 6-2. Earlier Sunday, the Atlanta Falcons lost their second straight game, falling 34-17 to the Cincinnati Bengals at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain. The loss dropped Atlanta to 3-6. How to watch Chiefs at Falcons Kickoff: Noon Central Where: Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -3.5 Behind the KC-ATL matchup The Chiefs and Falcons look a little different than they did last week, before the NFL’s trade deadline. Kansas City made the highly anticipated move Tuesday to acquire wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts . Meanwhile, Atlanta began the week by agreeing to trade three-time second-team All-Pro safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars before sending starting center Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens. Downs is expected to make his Chiefs debut Sunday in Atlanta. He recorded 33 catches for 354 yards and a touchdown for the Colts this season. Downs’ stat line included seven catches for 72 yards against Kansas City in Week 2. “I had to watch him live. Yeah, which wasn’t good,” Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Wednesday, drawing laughter from reporters. To earn extended playing time Sunday, Downs will have to demonstrate that he can handle Reid’s complex playbook. Kansas City kept that in mind while shopping for receivers. “That’s what we felt about Josh — that he has that ability,” Reid said. “And now it’s just a matter of him spending the time to knock it out. But he’s a pretty alert kid.” How Downs fits alongside Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy will be worth watching, but the good news for the Chiefs is that his debut should come with Patrick Mahomes under center. Mahomes suffered an injury scare late in the second quarter against the Jets. Mahomes hurt his elbow but remained in the game, and medical test results were encouraging. He was listed as a full participant in Wednesday’s practice. In an encouraging development, Worthy (hamstring) also participated fully. “I feel like I’m in a great spot,” Mahomes said. “Now it’s just about pain and pain management and stuff like that, which I’ll try to do whatever I can to be in the best place possible.” While much of the focus will be on Downs’ Chiefs debut and how Mahomes attacks a Falcons secondary playing its first game without Bates, the path to victory is likely to look familiar. Running back Kenneth Walker presents a favorable matchup against an Atlanta defense allowing 4.4 yards per carry. After two less productive games by his lofty standards, Walker rushed 18 times for 102 yards against the Jets , adding four receptions for 41 yards and three total touchdowns. Following his breakout performance in Denver, rookie Emmett Johnson rushed for 34 yards and a touchdown on six carries against New York. Asked about the Falcons’ defense, Reid highlighted edge rusher James Pearce, who returned last week for 15 snaps after serving an eight-game suspension to begin the season. The former first-round pick registered 10.5 sacks as a rookie in 2025. Pearce (back) missed practice Wednesday, so his status is worth monitoring. “(The Falcons are) fast — and even faster when they’re on their turf,” Reid said. “So they’re very athletic. They’ve got some young linebackers that are flying around. They’ve got that front, and they rotate those guys.” With right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) out of practice Wednesday, Josh Ezeudu could be in line to make his second start of the season. Pearce can line up on either side of the line, and he will be a challenge for both Ezeudu and Chiefs left tackle Kahlil Benson. The Falcons feature 11 players with at least one sack, including defensive end Za’Darius Smith (4.5), defensive end Cameron Thomas (2) and defensive tackle LaCale London (2) — all with at least two sacks on the season. On offense, the Falcons’ biggest threat is running back Bijan Robinson, the only player in the league with more rushing yards (880) than Walker (872), though with one additional game. “He’s electricity in a bottle,” Chiefs linebacker Nick Bolton said of Robinson. “That’s what I say. (He’s) able to change direction, get upfield, cutbacks. We see all the time everybody’s at the point of attack because he can cut it back and put pressure on the back-side corner on the outside zone to the opposite side. So he’s electricity in a bottle, like I said, and it’ll take all hands on deck.” Much like Kansas City, Atlanta wants its running game to create opportunities through the air. Robinson’s presence helps open things up for quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and wide receiver Drake London, who leads the Falcons with 692 receiving yards but only one touchdown. The Chiefs listed cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) as a full participant Wednesday, and his return after a two-game absence would help Kansas City match up against London. Kansas City’s defensive front will look to build on its momentum after sacking Jets quarterback Geno Smith five times last Sunday. Defensive end George Karlaftis and defensive tackle Chris Jones recorded two sacks apiece. According to NFL NextGen Stats, Penix posts a league-worst 34% completion percentage when under pressure. Jones should have an advantage over center Corey Levin, who is expected to make his first start of the season after replacing Neuzil. A sixth-round pick in 2017, Levin has spent most of his career in a reserve role. Despite kicker Harrison Butker’s recent struggles, Reid announced Wednesday that he would stick with him for now, with Justin Tucker waiting on the practice squad. Perhaps a homecoming for Butker, an Atlanta native, sparks the turnaround he’s been seeking. Chiefs-Falcons game prediction As evidenced by their respective deadline moves, the Chiefs are all in on 2026, as the Falcons look toward the future. Kansas City draws energy from Downs’ debut, Delane helps neutralize London and the pass rush builds on last week’s solid outing. Winner: Chiefs 27, Falcons 17 | Cover: Chiefs Sweeney’s record: (6-2-0) | Against the spread: (4-4-0) This story was originally published November 12, 2026 at 7:00 AM . home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have released their first injury report ahead of Week 10's game against the Atlanta Falcons. The Chiefs have quite a few injuries to consider heading into Week 10, but it's not nearly as bad as it could be. In fact, there are a few pleasant surprises. Both Patrick Mahomes and Xavier Worthy fully participated in practice on Wednesday . Worthy, in particular, feels like a blessing. He had a non-contact hamstring injury late in the fourth quarter of Week 9 vs. the Jets. Another pleasant surprise? A few more players are full participants after being limited in recent weeks. Here’s a quick breakdown of each team’s Week 10 injury report. Keep in mind that clubs can add to the injury report through kickoff on Sunday. They will release game status designations on Friday, Nov. 13. picks.headline: Texans vs. Browns Week 10 picks: Cleveland being treated like an afterthought
picks.blurb: Texans vs. Browns Week 10 picks: Cleveland being treated like an afterthought - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Poch leaving for Man U Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Skubal suitors emerge Texans vs. Browns Week 10 picks: Cleveland being treated like an afterthought Chris Pokorny · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 8:37 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns take on the Houston Texans this Sunday. The Browns are 3-0 at home this year, but after having lost two straight games, they are being treated like an afterthought this week. As you can see in the national picks below, not a single person is picking the Browns at home. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 10 game between the Browns and Texans: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Texans: Even sitting at 3-5, the Texans appear to be full steam ahead toward a playoff berth with the way their offense is playing and defense is improving. C.J. Stroud has Nick Caley's unit absolutely humming now that most of his main targets are healthy. The real key to that success is Nico Collins. In the 257 snaps Collins has played this season, the Texans have averaged 8.2 yards per passing play, more than the 49ers' league-leading 7.9. He could be stalled when matched up against cornerback Denzel Ward, who's allowing 0.5 yards per coverage snap, fifth-fewest among cornerbacks (min. 150 coverage snaps). That duel is sure to be dogfight Sunday, but no matter, as I have faith in Stroud's other weapons (Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison Jr., Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson) to get it done. Houston's lone offensive weakness matches up nicely against the Browns' permeable run defense. Getting Deshaun Watson back is a boost for Cleveland, but even with him, the Browns have struggled to put together a full game, instead relying on a few big plays each week from their young stars. An all-around performance is exactly what the Browns must have to beat the current version of DeMeco Ryans' team. Thus, Cleveland will fall short of improving to 4-0 at home for the first time since the 1963 campaign, when Jim Brown led the NFL in rushing and scrimmage yards in a 14-game season. CBS Sports (Pete Prisco) – Texans 21, Browns 20 This is a big game for both teams in terms of the playoff picture. The Texans looked dominant against the Chargers last week, but this is a second straight road game. It won't matter. Their defensive front will dominate whoever plays quarterback for the Browns. But the Cleveland defense will keep them in it. CBS Sports (John Breech) – Texans 24, Browns 16 Anyway, this genuinely does feel like a game that's going to boil down to Watson vs. the Texans. Watson has been sacked more times than any other QB in the NFL this year (33), and he'll be facing a defense that leads the NFL in sacks (29). That's a recipe for disaster. There have only been three games all season where a QB has been sacked at least eight times: Two of them were Deshaun Watson (vs. Jets in Week 5 and vs. Steelers in Week 8) and the other one happened on Sunday with the Texans sacking Justin Herbert eight times. Sporting News (Vinnie Iyer) – Texans 20, Browns 17 The Texans hope to sneak back into the playoff picture and their defense got back to making big plays in Los Angeles after the bye. Cleveland's defense will get a break as Houston is one-dimensional out of necessity, but in the end, old Texans friend Deshaun Watson will be outdueled by red-hot C.J. Stroud. Sporting News (Bill Bender) – Texans 22, Browns 19 Shedeur Sanders had 297 passing yards and two TDs in his first start of the season, and that might be enough to keep that in a home start against the Texans. Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud is coming off a 384-yard, five-TD performance against the Chargers. The Browns' early-season shine is wearing off, but they are 4-0 ATS as an underdog of seven points or less. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Houston Texans (3-5) head to Cleveland on Sunday looking to continue a dramatic midseason turnaround when they face the Browns (5-4) at Huntington Bank Field. The Texans opened the season with four straight losses but have won three of their last four. The division may be out of reach as the Jaguars lead the Texans by three games in the AFC South but Houston is back in the race for a Wild Card spot. Cleveland takes the field after dropping their last two games which has dropped them out of first in the AFC North and 1.5 games behind the Steelers and the Bengals. Houston is coming off its most explosive performance of the season, a 44-22 road rout of the winless Los Angeles Chargers. C.J. Stroud played through an illness and completed 21 of 35 passes for 384 yards, five touchdowns and one interception. He connected with four different players for scores, including 63-yard touchdowns to Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte , with Boutte finishing with 125 receiving yards and two touchdowns. The Texans led 24-9 at halftime, stretched the advantage to 38-9 early in the fourth quarter and defensively overwhelmed Justin Herbert , sacking him eight times. Cleveland arrives home following a gut-wrenching 23-22 overtime loss at New Orleans. With Deshaun Watson sidelined by a concussion, Shedeur Sanders started and finished 19-of-31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns, including a 64-yard go-ahead strike to KC Concepcion late in the fourth quarter. After New Orleans regained the lead, Andre Szmyt’s 51-yard field goal forced overtime. The Saints scored first in the extra period, but Sanders answered by finding Harold Fannin Jr. for a 39-yard touchdown before Cleveland went for two and the win; the conversion failed, dropping the Browns to 5-4. The matchup also renews a surprisingly balanced series. Houston leads the all-time matchup 8-7, including the postseason, but Cleveland won four consecutive meetings from 2020 through the 2023 regular season. Their most recent clash reversed that trend in emphatic fashion: in the 2023 AFC Wild Card round, Stroud threw for 274 yards and three touchdowns as Houston demolished Cleveland 45-14, with the Texans turning two Joe Flacco interceptions into defensive touchdowns. In addition to Watson’s health, other storylines include the Texans’ pass rush against Cleveland’s quarterback protection particularly after Sanders was sacked five times in New Orleans and Houston just recorded eight sacks against the Chargers. home.headline: Texans Injury Report vs. Browns Week 10: Multiple Starters Miss Practice
home.blurb: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans made it known that Montgomery's status has improved from last week ––when he was ruled out with a groin injury on Wednesday––but said he would continue to be evaluated throughout the week. It remains to be seen if he ends up playing once the weekend rolls around. Azeez Al-Shaair might be a name to keep an eye on, as he was a DNP with seemingly the same groin injury that's restricted his availability in practice as of late . However, given that he also had a personal designation, there's a better chance that he'll be good to go for either Thursday or Friday's session. Tight end Brevin Jordan also wound up as a DNP in practice with a finger/foot issue. If he's unable to go against the Browns, Houston has four other tight ends on the roster to turn to instead, including second-round rookie Marlin Klein, who was active on the gameday against the LA Chargers for the first time since Week 4. The Texans' final status for everyone on the roster will become clearer after Friday's practice. But until then, keep a close watch on those four who didn't practice, while also not losing sight of anyone who was limited for Wednesday’s action. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run? This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Commanders +2.5): The last time these two teams faced off, they TIED. I'm expecting another close game and may be leaning toward the underdog. Washington played the Los Angeles Rams tough last Sunday and held Matthew Stafford and Co. to 20 points. J.J. McCarthy has looked solid with his new team, but he actually just became the only quarterback in the past 40 seasons to register a win with zero passing touchdowns in four straight starts (dating back to last year). He suffered a hip injury vs. the Philadelphia Eagles , while Cam Skattebo is coming off a hamstring strain. Both will play, but I do wonder how much those issues could linger. The Commanders are 4-0-1 straight up and 4-1 against the spread (ATS) in their last five against the New York Giants , so I'll take the points here in a potential upset. … Prediction: Commanders 21, Giants 20 Dubin (Giants -2.5): I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith that this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. … Prediction: Giants 20, Commanders 14 New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions (-2.5) (Munich) Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20 Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late. … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21 Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17 Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game. … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14 San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) at Dallas Cowboys Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26 Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Christopher Gates · SB Nation Tue, November 10, 2026 at 2:13 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After falling out of first place in the NFC North for the first time this season, the Minnesota Vikings will look to avoid moving into the division's basement when they head to Lambeau Field in Week 10 to conclude their home-and-home series with the Green Bay Packers for this season. The people who set the betting lines, apparently, don't like their chances. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the lines for Sunday's game, and the Vikings currently sit as a 4.5-point underdog to the Packers. The over/under for the game currently rests at 42.5 points. The Vikings, as we all saw on Monday Night Football, appear to have completely abandoned the concept of offense, as they generated none of it in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills for their second loss in a row. Carson Wentz stepped in at quarterback for the injured Kyler Murray and turned in what may have been the worst start a Vikings quarterback has put together in recent memory, completing just 8-of-25 passes and turning the ball over three times, including two interceptions. . .a number that could have been significantly higher. The Packers, on the other hand, have won five of their last six after getting off to a 1-2 start. This past week, they absolutely thumped the New England Patriots to the tune of 45-27 behind three more touchdown passes from Jordan Love and a defense that forced Drake Maye into three interceptions. The Packers currently sit in last place in the North, but with a 6-3 record would lead either the NFC South or the NFC East. . .that's just how good the NFC North has been this season. These two teams met in the regular season opener at U.S. Bank Stadium. Wentz came into the game midway through the first quarter after Murray suffered a concussion, and the Packers had a 22-10 lead with just over five minutes remaining in the third quarter. From there, however, the Minnesota defense took over, leading an onslaught against Love and the Green Bay offense that saw the Vikings score 29 unanswered points to finish the game, including forcing a turnover on downs and generating an interception and a fumble to set up scoring opportunities. Minnesota took home the 39-22 win to get their season off to a 1-0 start. With the NFL trade deadline looming at 3:00 PM Central today. . .or approximately seven hours from when this story goes up. . .we will see if anything the Vikings do (or don't do) will shift this number at all. As it stands now, however, the Vikings are currently an underdog to their division rivals as the second half of the season officially gets underway.

picks.headline: Packers vs. Vikings Odds: Opening line for Week 10 matchup
picks.blurb: Packers vs. Vikings Odds: Opening line for Week 10 matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Poch leaving for Man U Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Skubal suitors emerge Packers vs. Vikings Odds: Opening line for Week 10 matchup (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Justis Mosqueda · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 6:40 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers (6-3) are set to be three-point favorites over the Minnesota Vikings (6-1) in Week 10, according to FanDuel's numbers . That number comes with a little juice at -120, and the Packers are -178 favorites, which comes with an implied probability of 64 percent. If you had said this a few weeks ago, when the Packers' offensive line was drowning, no one would have bought it. Now, after Green Bay finally had a 100-yard rushing performance and beat down on the New England Patriots in all three phases of the game, it looks like the Packers have a real opportunity to make a push for the postseason. The Vikings have played two fewer games than the Packers because: 1) they've already had their bye week and 2) they're playing on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. After that game, they'll have a short(er) week and have to travel on the road to Lambeau Field. Their starting quarterback, Kyler Murray, is currently dealing with a hamstring injury and will not play against the Bills. We'll have to see if it heals up by the time they kick off against the Packers, or if it'll be Carson Wentz — their current replacement starter — under center. The only other quarterback in Minnesota is Max Brosmer (53-man roster). Below is the current playoff picture in the NFC: San Francisco 49ers: 7-1 (NFC West) Minnesota Vikings: 6-1 (NFC North) New York Giants: 5-2-1 (NFC East) Carolina Panthers: 3-5 (NFC South) Chicago Bears: 7-2 Detroit Lions: 6-2 Green Bay Packers: 6-3 Seattle Seahawks: 5-4 Los Angeles Rams: 5-4 Dallas Cowboys: 4-5 New Orleans Saints: 3-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 3-6 Atlanta Falcons: 3-6 Arizona Cardinals: 3-6 Washington Commanders: 2-5-1 Philadelphia Eagles: 2-7 The Packers are holding onto the seventh seed right now, where they've been for weeks, but the NFC North keeps winning — as do the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams, the teams trying to hunt them down from behind. The NFC is so wonky, with the "good" teams being in the North and West, not the South and East, that the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers currently have about as good a chance of making the playoffs (by winning the NFC South) as do the Los Angeles Rams (a .500 team that is essentially locked into a playoff spot or nothing in 2026), per The Athletic's playoff simulator . In short, there are seven North and West teams fighting for five playoff spots in the NFC, and then there's whatever the hell is happening in the East and South. Do not be surprised at all if a sub-.500 NFC South team ends up hosting a 12-5 (or better record) NFC North team in the wild card round this year.

picks.headline: Week 10 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Kirk Cousins returns to lead Vikings vs. Packers
picks.blurb: Week 10 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Kirk Cousins returns to lead Vikings vs. Packers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Poch leaving for Man U Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Skubal suitors emerge Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, November 12, 2026 at 1:48 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It wasn't that long ago that Kirk Cousins, in his first stint with the Minnesota Vikings, was the quarterback who could never win the big one . Everyone remembers this critique of him. These days, Kirk Cousins is 38. And somehow, everyone spent days and weeks arguing that the only way for the Vikings to have a chance to win the big one was to trade for Cousins. That trade did happen, and it was perfectly reasonable for the Vikings to see if Cousins can guide them to an NFC North title and maybe a playoff run. They have the defense for it but we saw on Monday night that the offense was beyond repair with the quarterback situation they had. Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell was hesitant to announce Cousins would start Sunday against the Green Bay Packers, but the Vikings didn't trade for Cousins to watch Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz start in a huge divisional game. While the trade for Cousins was reasonable, the Vikings still have the fourth-best quarterback in the division and the fourth-best offense in the division as well. Cousins is an upgrade but mostly because the Vikings had a dreadful quarterback situation. The Packers didn't do anything at the trade deadline but it might be because they've been on quite a roll. They were not good through three weeks but somehow have emerged as one of the better teams in the NFL since then. Since Week 4, they're fourth in EPA ( expected points added ) per play on offense and third in EPA per play allowed on defense. It's a good team. Anyone will have issues with the Vikings' defense and we'll see if the Packers' deep passing game can function against Minnesota's many blitzes. But Packers -3 is the pick. Taking the Vikings and Cousins, five days after rejoining the team, against a red-hot team is too much to ask. New Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) shown facing the Packers in a 2023 game. Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 10 of the NFL season: Commanders (+2.5) over Giants The Giants are three games up on the Commanders in the NFC East, but New York isn't that great. The Commanders come in as the more desperate team. Their season is all but over if they lose on Thursday. That's not the best reason to pick a team, but it's good enough in a game between two flawed teams. Patriots (+2.5) over Lions This is the NFL's last early-morning game of the season. The Lions and Patriots meet in Germany. The Patriots are coming off a bad loss to the Packers, and have their running back issues with Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson out. One factor to consider is the Lions aren't the same team outdoors. Jared Goff's rating in domes is 102.9 and outdoors it is 92.4. There is some noise in those numbers, and Goff's ratings haven't had that big of a gap the past two seasons, but Detroit also just scored 19 points at Miami last week. That and the Lions' defensive deficiencies are enough to take the Patriots and the points. Texans (-4.5) over Browns The Browns have a better record, but also a -35 point differential. It's not like the Texans have been great, but there's a path for them to make the playoffs. They also know they can't drop games like this one. C.J. Stroud is playing well enough that points shouldn't be too hard for Houston to come by. Titans (+10.5) over Jaguars The Jaguars have taken over as my Super Bowl pick after the deadline. However, 10.5 is a lot of points in the NFL and the Titans have played three close games in a row. They're coming off their bye and have some extra rest. The Jaguars can't blow everyone out, right? Colts (-3.5) over Dolphins It's very hard to take the Colts, especially because the Dolphins are playing hard. The Colts played hard last week, but have to be deflated after losing that game to the Cowboys in the final minutes and seeing more players traded away. But it's even harder to back new Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord, a 2025 sixth-round pick who has never taken an NFL snap, playing with a subpar group. McCord gets the start for Miami with Malik Willis on injured reserve. Jets (+8) over Bills Talk about an ugly NFL side to take. The Jets are not good. But the Bills are coming off a physical game in Minnesota on Monday night and now go on the road to face the Jets on short rest. It seems unwise to take the Jets, but point spreads exist for a reason. Panthers (+2.5) over Saints The Saints are probably better in theory than reality. They won last week, but needed to defend a two-point conversion in overtime to knock off Shedeur Sanders and the Browns. It feels like the Saints have the potential to be the best team in the NFC South, but there's not much evidence they are. The Panthers are in a slump but have been the better team. Chiefs (-3.5) over Falcons It's not like the Falcons trading Jessie Bates III makes them significantly worse, but it's a difficult message for the locker room. It makes it seem like the front office is waving the white flag. In reality they got an offer they couldn't turn down, but it's still worth wondering how the remaining players will react. And Kansas City is a pretty good team. Cardinals (+9.5) over Rams For the rest of the season, or at least until Puka Nacua or Davante Adams returns, the Rams will try to survive by running the ball and playing defense in low-scoring games. There's not much explosiveness in the offense without any dangerous receivers. That will make them tough to back when the spread is large. Can Carson Beck lead the Arizona offense to enough points against a good Rams defense to cover any spread? That's the key question. Seahawks (-6.5) over Raiders This isn't a pick due to Fernando Mendoza facing the Seahawks defense, though that is a factor. It's because the Raiders defense is horrible. Since Week 3, after the Raiders had faced the offensively challenged Dolphins and Chargers, they're last in the NFL in EPA by a wide margin. They're 32nd in yards allowed and points allowed. The Seahawks will be able to move the ball, even with Drew Lock at quarterback. 49ers (-4.5) over Cowboys There are no signs the Cowboys are ready to have some kind of breakout. Last week they almost lost to a Colts team that has already given up on the season. And now they're supposed to keep it close against the 49ers, who have arguably been the best team in the NFL? Steelers (+3.5) over Bengals The Joe Burrow-for-MVP bandwagon is still running , but it's hard to lay more than a field goal in what should be a great divisional game. The Steelers can run the ball, and run defense is a weakness of the Bengals. They're last in the NFL in yards allowed per carry. Also, the Steelers are coming off a bye while the Bengals are coming off a game in Paris, which is the type of massive rest disadvantage that the NFL should do a better job avoiding. The Bengals are good but this isn't a great matchup or a good spot for them. Ravens (-4.5) over Chargers The Chargers will cover a spread this season. They haven't yet. They are the last team in the NFL to not cover the spread this season. But we'll take that loss when it comes because proactively taking the truly miserable Chargers in hopes they finally cover is not an enjoyable exercise. Also, the Ravens have three days of extra rest and perhaps a little bit of renewed hope with Jacoby Brissett coming aboard. Last week: 9-6 Season to date: 62-71-2
