picks.blurb: Vikings vs. Packers bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Poch leaving for Man U Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Skubal suitors emerge Vikings vs. Packers bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 10 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Thu, November 12, 2026 at 7:55 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings made a big-deal trade. And the details caught Packers head coach Matt LaFleur by surprise. Now these teams meet in a Week 10 NFC North battle, and here are bold predictions for the contest. The Vikings enter with a 6-2 record, while the Packers sit last in the division despite a 6-3 mark. It's a different setting than it would have been before the trade deadline, as the Vikings dramatically improved their QB situation. They grabbed Kirk Cousins in a deal with the Raiders. Will he shine in his second debut with the Vikings? Vikings QB Kirk Cousins will throw for 225-plus yards and two TDs Let's face it. If the Vikings don't put the ball in the air against the Packers, they're very unlikely to win. The Packers are going to score some points, even against that tough Vikings defense. So Cousins has to come out balling. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) And there's really no reason for Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell to hold Cousins back, according to startribune.com. "When there's completions to be had, he's going to find them," O'Connell said. "That can be down the field, that can be in the intermediate areas, that can be checkdowns. Kirk is a quarterback that's understood and progressed at a high level to a place of the power of completion, what it does to a defense, what it does to his teammates, what it does to the rhythm of the offense. "That's a unique thing, because he can understand the intent of a play, what we're trying to get done and then how to attack that and play fast." And Cousins said he's anxious to get a fresh start with the Vikings. "To be back there, wearing the purple and gold, it has meaning," Cousins said. "But you have to go make it mean something with the way you play." And the player-coach relationship matters. "Kevin knows me," Cousins said. "(He) knows what I do well. Kevin knows what I don't do well. Kevin knows what I can handle, what I can't handle, and I think that helps." Packers QB Jordan Love will hit three 30-plus-yard plays Remember, this is a good defense. But the Packers aren't going to stop doing what they do based on the Vikings' abilities. Also, the big plays don't have to come on long passes down the field. Love can hit Matthew Golden or Christian Watson against the blitz, and they can break into the clear for a big gain. The Packers have to keep attacking , Love said, according to Packers.com. "Against this defense, you know what it is, you can't get frustrated," Love said. "There's going to be some times where they get you, or the call we got just isn't good enough versus what they're bringing. "That's part of it. They'll win some reps for sure, and you just gotta stay focused." The Vikings are going to heat the Packers up. They lead the NFL with a 72.5% blitz rate on passing downs. And they do it from many angles. Toss in the fact that the Packers will have to deal with the crowd noise, and it's quite a challenge. "Oh, man, it makes a huge difference," Love said of playing in the Vikings dome. "Silent count, it's easier for D-line to get a little bit of a get-off. They kind of know what's coming. But I think, too, just playing there, the environment, the noise, all those things, it throws communication off for an offense. We can't hear each other." But the reason Love will hit several big plays is his ability to carve up a blitz. He leads the NFL in passing yards against the blitz (967) and is tied for first in passing TDs with 10. "His anticipation to see space and just trust his receivers and get the ball into wherever area that's supposed to be has been pretty awesome," Vikings offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich. "Whether that's layering a ball, giving it some time or throwing it on a line, it's been pretty impressive to watch. "He's calm, doesn't get rattled, so he's just a special player when it comes to that." Vikings WR Justin Jefferson will set season high in yardage This is a strong bet for two reasons. First, Jefferson set his season high of 92 yards against the Packers. He also scored twice. Since then, Jefferson has one TD and 301 yards in six other games. He'll bounce back because Cousins is going to find ways to get him the ball. away.headline: Vikings-Bills Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray is out as expected, as are both Demond Claiborne and Jauan Jennings. Claiborne suffered a knee injury in practice and from Kevin O’Connell’s comments on Saturday, could be out for a while. It wouldn’t be surprising therefore if he was placed on Injured Reserve. It doesn’t appear at the moment that Jennings’ calf injury is a longer-term concern, but we may learn more about that next week. Beyond that, safeties Theo Jackson and Jay Ward are questionable for Monday night. I’m guessing at least one of them will play, but KOC also talked about potentially having Jacob Thomas and/or Tavierre Thomas on the active roster for Monday night to fill in at safety and special teams. For the Bills, backup wide receiver Joshua Palmer is out. But they also have two starting offensive linemen listed as questionable- left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson. Dawkins has not practiced all week with a rib injury, so he would seem to be less likely than normal to start with that designation. Anderson was upgraded to limited on Saturday after missing Thursday and Friday practices with an ankle injury. My guess is that if either of them play on Monday night they will be less than 100%, so the left side of the Bills’ offensive line could be a bit more vulnerable than normal. Beyond that, Tyrell Shavers and Jordan Hancock are listed as questionable, but the Bills will need to activate them from the PUP list and IR for them to be eligible to play on Monday night. We’ll see if that happens. home.headline: Injury timeline emerges for Packers RB Josh Jacobs
home.blurb: Packers medical staff tried multiple methods to protect Jacobs’ hand in hopes of getting him back on the field, but he was ultimately unable to return. Jacobs will undergo surgery to repair the issue sometime later this week. According to a report from NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport, he could return to the field for the Packers as quickly as 2-3 weeks. The earliest opportunity for Jacobs’ return is a Week 12 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams. While Jacobs could be back in a couple weeks, there’s also a chance his absence extends for a longer period. If the Packers decide to place him on injured reserve this weekend, he’ll automatically be ruled out for the team’s next four games. If that’s the case, his earliest opportunity to return would be a Week 15 matchup against the Miami Dolphins. Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs fractured his ring finger during the first quarter of this past Sunday’s Week 9 win over the New England Patriots. Green Bay is set for a division-rival matchup against the Minnesota Vikings this coming weekend. After that, the team will enter its Week 11 bye. Jacobs missed the first six games of the Packers’ 2026 campaign on the Commissioner’s Exempt List. The veteran running back recorded three total touchdowns in his two full games back on the field in Weeks 7 and 8. Backup RB Kaleb Johnson stepped up following Jacobs’ exit against the Patriots, rushing for 68 yards and a touchdown on 14 carries. The Packers, led by quarterback Jordan Love, furthered their reputation as one of the best passing offenses in the league. The Packers will kick off against the Vikings at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. home.headline: Josh Jacobs injury update: New development emerges on Packers star RB
home.blurb: Although Jacobs will undergo surgery later this week and is already ruled out for Sunday’s matchup against the Minnesota Vikings, his potential recovery timeline is shorter than initially feared. Jacobs could return in as little as two to three weeks, giving Green Bay hope that he won’t need an extended absence. Josh Jacobs could return in 2-3 weeks after surgery An injured reserve designation would require Jacobs to miss at least four games. Avoiding that decision would give the Packers more flexibility and potentially allow their starting running back to return much sooner. Green Bay has its bye following the Vikings game, meaning part of Jacobs’ recovery period will overlap with a week when the team isn’t playing. Rapoport indicated that Jacobs could have a chance to return after the bye, depending on how his recovery progresses. The Green Bay Packers have received encouraging news regarding Josh Jacobs after the running back suffered a broken ring finger against the New England Patriots in NFL Week 9. MORE: Top 10 NFL teams: Rankings updated after trade deadline According to Rapoport, Jacobs could be back on the field within two to three weeks following surgery on his broken ring finger. The Packers are expected to make a decision Saturday on whether to place him on injured reserve, but that move is not guaranteed. The latest update is encouraging considering the uncertainty surrounding Jacobs after head coach Matt LaFleur initially declined to provide a recovery timeline. LaFleur confirmed that surgery was necessary after Jacobs struggled to grip the football following the injury. MORE: Bold predictions for Week 10 of 2026 NFL season Packers will be without Jacobs against Vikings Jacobs will miss Sunday’s divisional matchup against Minnesota, but the timing of the Packers’ upcoming bye could work in his favor. The Packers will need other running backs to step up in his absence. Kaleb Johnson, Pierre Strong Jr. and potentially MarShawn Lloyd could help handle the workload against Minnesota. For Packers fans, the biggest takeaway is that Jacobs may not be facing a lengthy absence. The possibility of a two-to-three-week recovery gives Green Bay reason for optimism, although the team’s Saturday decision on injured reserve will be an important development to monitor.

picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars vs. Titans: Which New Addition Makes the First Big Play Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- After a frantic start to the week that saw the Jacksonville Jaguars make the biggest moves of this year's NFL Trade Deadline, it is worth remember that the Jaguars do, in fact, have an opponent on Sunday. The 6-2 Jaguars are set to travel to Nissan Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, their first game since making blockbuster trades for Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, along with adding Davon Godchaux for a sixth-round pick. For a Jaguars team that has their eyes set on an AFC South title and a top seed in the playoffs, they are treating the Titans with the same seriousness that they treated the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens over the last two weeks. So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 10 battle with the Titans playing out? We break it down below. Jessie Bates Records An Interception While it certainly remains to be seen if the Jaguars will actually play any of their new defensive pieces against the Titans, I believe they will. Jakobi Meyers and Greg Newsome each played in their first games with the franchise last season after joining the team during that same week, and I think that means we see the trio make their Jaguars debuts. In the process, I think we see Bates create his first Jaguars takeaway right off the bat. Cam Ward is far from the most turnover-prone quarterback the Jaguars have played this season; that distinction goes to Daniel Jones. But he is right near the league average in interception rate, and he has made some egregious decisions with the ball over his last two seasons as a starter. This feels like the perfect week for Anthony Campanile to cook some pressure looks up to confuse Ward, and Bates is a natural playmaker. I think we see his impact right away. Parker Washington Catches 2 TDs The Titans' defense has been ... not very good against slot receivers this season. The Titans rank in the bottom-5 in the NFL against slot targets in each of the following categories: yards per play allowed, yards after the catch allowed, yards after the catch over expectation, and average seperation. The Titans have simply been a mess in the slot, even moving long-time outside cornerback Alontae Taylor to the slot despite signing him in March to play on the outside. As a result, I think this is a Parker Washington week. He is the clear No. 1 receiver in the offense, and I think he shakes off some inconsistent moments we have seen as of late and has a huge game against the Titans. Washington is due for a big performance, and I think we see it this Sunday against the Titans. Cam Ward Throws For Fewer Than 150 Yards There have been 275 quarterback performances this season. In just 39 of those performances, we have seen quarterbacks throw for fewer than 150 yards. Cam Ward makes up two of those games, a number that is trumped only by Bo Nix and Malis Willis which is, well, not great company to be in as far as productive gunslingers go. Ward has been more productive and explosive as of late and is coming off one of the best games of his career, but I predict the Jaguars limit Ward to under 150. Ward threw for just 141 yards against the Jaguars in Week 13 a year ago, and the Jaguars limited Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano to a combined 189 yards over the last eight quarters. The Jaguars' pass defense is clicking, largely due to the work of defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, and I believe we see it continue this week. Jaguars Limit Tony Pollard to Under 4.0 YPC Titans running back Tony Pollard has been on a tear over the last few weeks. Pollard, who has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns over the last two games, broke out of a mid-season skid and has been able to average over 4.0 yards per carry in every single game but two this season. While Pollard has been one of the NFL's more impressive runners over the last few weeks, I expect the Jaguars to be ready to bottle him up on Sunday. Again, I think the Jaguars will play Davis and Godchaux on Sunday. But even if they don't, I do not think the Titans have the offense to keep the Jaguars off-balance enough to run the ball on them. Teams can only run the ball on the Jaguars when the Jaguars are threatened by the early-down pass, and I do not see the Titans having much success there. Walker Little Pitches Another Shutout The Jaguars have seen Walker Little play really, really well over the last few weeks since stepping into the lineup for an injured Anton Harrison. According to NextGenStats, Little has allowed pressure on just 6.4% of his pass blocks, the fifth lowest rate in the league among left tackles (minimum 100 pass blocks). On his 109 pass blocks, his 87.2% 1-on-1 matchup rate is the highest in the league among left tackles; his 6.3% 1-on-1 pressure rate allowed is the third lowest pressure rate allowed in the league. “The experience always helps. Confidence is a heck of a thing, and I think he's the one that said it in an interview that humility helped. Where obviously he became our swing tackle, and all that guy has done is just stay the course," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "Like, never got up, too down. He's just very steady. I really like Walker's play demeanor, the look in his eye recently and not taking everything so seriously. He's able to have fun with it. He's out there playing a game that he loves and competes with, but he's playing at a high level right now. He's got confidence, and you can tell.” Little will mostly draw Titans pass-rusher Jacob Martin, who has had a good year. But after strong showings against the Houston Texans' pass-rush duo in London a month ago and then a dominant outing against Trey Hendrickson last week , I think Little has the edge entering Week 10. He is playing some of the best football of his career right now, and I predict it leads to another shutout. Fans wouldn't be blamed for forgetting that we've got football this coming Sunday after days on end filled with rumors and breaking news at the end of every sentence. Not only do the Titans play in Week 10, but they're hosting AFC South-rivals. The Jacksonville Jaguars, one of the most active buyers at the trade deadline, are coming to Nashville to boast their new pickups. The last time Tennessee faced Jacksonville, the Titans lost 41-7 at the very end of the 2025 season. Cam Ward missed the majority of that game after exiting early with a shoulder injury, and his healthy showing tomorrow is the key to a potential Titans upset. Will: Cam Ward stays hot in Carnell Tate's return Ward nearly led Tennessee to a victory over the (now) 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. The Titans falling short 36-43 in overtime was partly due to Ward taking a costly sack late in regulation, but the QB can't at all be blamed for losing a game he kept Tennessee in. With WR1 Carnell Tate trending toward a return, Ward should have all of his weapons in place to put up another promising game. The Titans even kept RB Tony Pollard at the deadline for Ward's own sake. Again, Jacksonville bulked up at the deadline - their defense specifically - but Tennessee leaving the offense untouched said loud and clear that this franchise believes in Ward. With a newly-gutted defense, the Titans will be relying on Ward to try and secure the win. Won't: Jaguars' overhauled defense clicks immediately Directly opposing Ward is that new-look Jags defense. In addition to adding All-Pro S Jessie Bates III, Jacksonville also acquired defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. Oct 25, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III (3) reacts after an interception with safety Xavier Watts (31) against the San Francisco 49ers during the fourth quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The south-most AFC South team sold off a ton of draft potential to make this happen, but the 6-2 team got a whole lot better as they sprint toward a hopeful Super Bowl appearance. Two out of the next three weeks, the Titans stand in the way. The south-most AFC South team sold off a ton of draft potential to make this happen, but the 6-2 team got a whole lot better as they sprint toward a hopeful Super Bowl appearance. Two out of the next three weeks, the Titans stand in the way. FOX Sports already had Jacksonville listed as a top 10 defensive team in the NFL prior to these trades. If Tennessee falls short (as is likely expected), it will be because the Jaguars' defense put a stopper in Ward and the offense's growth. That could be one reason among many, but it seems to be the most relevant by far regarding this specific matchup. Prediction: Titans lose, 34-23 At the end of the day on Sunday, I expect Jacksonville will overwhelm Tennessee. I don't believe it will be in blowout fashion, and this is primarily because of the stable flashes of progress Ward showed in Week 8. But between their overhauled defense and Trevor Lawrence manning things under center on offense, the Titans are truly facing a championship contender this week. Perhaps the home field will help blunt the blow, as well as the team debuting their Music City jerseys. I love the jerseys. I like what we saw from Cam Ward in his most recent game. But this Jaguars team has the AFC South in a headlock, and the 1-7 Titans simply don't have enough on paper to climb out of a double-digit projected loss in this one. Tennessee Titans (1-7). The Jaguars have won five of their last six and are coming off consecutive blowout victories. The Titans were off last weekend but take the field having dropped two straight since recording their only victory of the season at Indianapolis back in mid-October. As is the case in most NFL games, the spotlight shines the brightest on the quarterbacks as we approach gameday. Trevor Lawrence is flourishing having thrown for 1,932 yards, 18 touchdowns and only four interceptions. He is an MVP candidate. Tennessee’s Cam Ward continues to labor under center having thrown for 1,483 yards with only six touchdowns and yet five interceptions. His future with Tennessee looks uncertain. Jacksonville’s latest performance was a convincing 33-10 Thursday-night victory at Baltimore, its second straight win by at least 23 points. Lawrence completed 16 of 26 passes for 242 yards and delivered the game’s biggest offensive play, a 50-yard touchdown to Parker Washington late in the second quarter that sent Jacksonville into halftime ahead 17-3. The Jaguars limited Baltimore to 227 total yards, forced three turnovers and kept the Ravens out of the red zone entirely; Baltimore’s only touchdown came on a 65-yard Justice Hill run in the fourth quarter with Jacksonville already leading 33-3. As noted earlier, Tennessee had its bye last week. It came at an ideal time after an exhausting 43-36 overtime loss at Cincinnati, arguably its best offensive showing of the season despite another defeat. The Titans jumped ahead 13-0 and took a 36-29 advantage with just 3:46 remaining when Ward hit Wan’Dale Robinson for a 15-yard touchdown and converted the ensuing two-point try, but Cincinnati tied the game with 1:17 left and won in overtime on Joe Burrow’s nine-yard touchdown run. Ward produced his first career 300-yard passing game, completing 26 of 40 for 304 yards and two touchdowns, while Tony Pollard ran 21 times for 117 yards and two scores. Tennessee accumulated 440 yards and forced four turnovers, including three interceptions by safety Amani Hooker , yet its defense was shredded for 510 yards and allowed Burrow to throw for 462 yards and five touchdowns before his overtime rushing score. The rivalry adds another layer because Jacksonville has emphatically reversed what was once a Tennessee-dominated series. The Titans still lead 35-28 all time, including their famous 33-14 victory over Jacksonville in the 1999 AFC Championship Game, but the Jaguars have won four consecutive meetings and seven of the last 10. Jacksonville swept Tennessee in each of the past two seasons, including a 25-3 win in Nashville last November and a 41-7 rout in Jacksonville on Jan. 4, 2026, the largest Jaguars victory in the history of the rivalry. picks.headline: Titans scouting report vs Jacksonville Jaguars, matchups, prediction NFL Week 10
picks.blurb: News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals TITANS Titans scouting report vs Jacksonville Jaguars, matchups, prediction NFL Week 10 Tyler Palmateer Nashville Tennessean Nov. 11, 2026, 5:02 a.m. CT With a 1-7 record, the Titans' focus for the rest of the season is on player evaluation. The Jacksonville Jaguars lead the AFC South and have strengthened their defense with recent trades. Trading Jeffery Simmons changed everything. The Tennessee Titans quietly submitted to a lost 2026 NFL season by dealing their eighth-year All-Pro defensive tackle to the Chicago Bears on Oct. 29. Tennessee general manager Mike Borgonzi then reinforced the team's desire to build for the future by trading eighth-year veteran safety Amani Hooker to the Buffalo Bills on Nov. 10. Barring a miraculous playoff push without their top two defenders, rivalry points seem to be all that matter for the Titans (1-7) in Week 10 against the Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) at Nissan Stadium on Nov. 15 (noon CT, FOX). The Titans’ final nine-game stretch will be about observations. Will quarterback Cam Ward play more like a franchise quarterback to finish his second season? Will star rookies Carnell Tate and Anthony Hill Jr. maintain their pace? Who are becoming pieces for Borgonzi’s long-term vision? Finding a way to win one-score games — the Titans have lost six — can help answer those questions regardless of the team’s final record. The Jaguars have won five of their past six games and have a three-game lead in the AFC South. They enhanced their defense this week by trading for All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III from the Atlanta Falcons and 10th-year defensive tackle Davon Godchaux from the New Orleans Saints. Here’s our scouting report for the Titans’ game against the Jaguars. One Jacksonville Jaguars stat to know: 28 That’s career interceptions for Bates. He’ll be a factor. He has at least one interception in each of his nine NFL seasons. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Jaguars Is Ward really the Titans’ only hope? He takes a lot of criticism, some deserved. But why can’t he be an advantage this time? He played at an elite level with a career-high 304 yards passing and two TDs against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. A Ward hot streak in November may be Tennessee’s best chance. The Jaguars rank 21st in the league in passing yards allowed per game (229.0). That’s one spot lower than Cincinnati. There’s an opportunity for Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll to give Ward more downfield throws as he did against the Bengals. Where Jacksonville Jaguars have edge vs. Titans Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence could have a big day against the Titans’ secondary, which was already leaky and now lacks its best player in Hooker. Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals shredded Tennessee with 462 yards passing, three touchdowns and nine plays of 18 yards or more. He was intercepted three times, but all of those came from Hooker. Aside from Alontae Taylor's solid debut at nickel cornerback against the Bengals, other parts of the secondary displayed poor tackling and bad angles. Tennessee ranks 31st in the NFL in passing yards allowed (258.3). Lawrence has thrown for 1,932 yards, 18 touchdowns and four interceptions. He's first in the league with 8.6 yards per pass among active quarterbacks with at least 100 dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus. Jaguars receiver Parker Washington has 493 yards on 29 catches and is ninth among league receivers with five touchdowns. He ranks third at 17 yards per catch. Matchup to watch Titans defensive end Jacob Martin versus Jaguars left tackle Walker Little. Martin is Tennessee’s best pass rusher with Simmons gone. He had three sacks against the Bengals and has 6.5 for the season. The Jaguars have shuffled their left tackle spot this season. Little has made only three starts, but he didn’t allow a single pressure or sack in last week’s 33-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. Score prediction: Jaguars 28, Titans 21 Ward and the Titans' offense will maintain their recent progress. But Tennessee's inability to finish games will also continue. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Miami Dolphins (1-7) and Indianapolis Colts (2-7) meet Sunday at Lucas Oil Stadium in a matchup between two teams racing towards the top of the 2027 Draft. The Dolphins have lost two straight and sit in the cellar in the AFC East while the Colts have lost five in a row and have only the Titans between them and a spot in the basement in the AFC South. The headline as these teams take the field is that Miami’s starting signal-caller, Malik Willis , has been placed on the IR and as a result, rookie Kyle McCord will get the first start of his career. Indianapolis will continue with Daniel Jones , who has 1,722 passing yards and six touchdowns this season. Jones, however, has struggled to regain the form he had prior to tearing his Achilles late last season. Miami’s latest setback was a 19-9 home loss to the Detroit Lions, a game in which the Dolphins’ defense did enough to give the offense a chance but Miami never reached the end zone. Willis completed just 13 of 25 passes for 128 yards with an interception, while Ollie Gordon II led the Dolphins with 55 rushing yards and Caleb Douglas caught six passes for 70 yards. Miami finished with only 228 total yards, went 0-for-3 in the red zone and settled for three Zane Gonzalez field goals. Indianapolis’ last loss was considerably more painful. The Colts rallied from a 17-7 halftime deficit against Dallas, getting a 55-yard touchdown catch from Ashton Dulin and field goals of 59 and 50 yards from Spencer Shrader to take a 23-20 lead with 1:37 remaining. But Dak Prescott immediately hit Ryan Flournoy for 46 yards, and Javonte Williams scored from a yard out with 1:08 left to give Dallas a 27-23 victory. Jones finished 20-of-34 for 180 yards, a touchdown and an interception, while Jonathan Taylor managed only 46 yards on 13 carries and lost a costly fourth-quarter fumble. Dallas piled up 508 yards to Indianapolis’ 271, illustrating the biggest concern for a Colts’ team that is allowing 361.8 yards and 27.7 points per game. The central storyline, then, is which struggling offense can take advantage of an accommodating opponent. Miami is averaging only 15.8 points per game, 31st in the league, and will be asking McCord to make his debut on the road; Indianapolis averages 20.4 points but carries a -11 turnover differential, making ball security especially important for Jones and Taylor. Recent history favors the Colts. Indianapolis has won the last three meetings, including a 33-8 rout at Lucas Oil Stadium in Week 1 of the 2025 season, when Jones completed 22 of 29 passes for 272 yards and a touchdown and Taylor rushed for 71 yards. The broader history belongs to the Dolphins, who hold a 48-30 advantage across 78 regular-season and postseason meetings. 5 bold Colts predictions that could turn the Dolphins game upside down
picks.blurb: 5 bold Colts predictions that could turn the Dolphins game upside down Skip to main content News FanSided NFL Sites It’s been a roller-coaster of a year for the Indianapolis Colts. The team entered the season with hopes of contending for a division title, but now finds itself in a full-on rebuild. In the last few weeks, the Colts have fired their general manager, traded away key players, and lost five straight games. At this point, expecting any good news for Indianapolis would qualify as a “bold prediction”. But, the Colts have a chance to stop the bleeding in Week 10 when they host the 1-win Miami Dolphins — one of the only teams that’s just as much of a disaster as them. This is the perfect opportunity for Indianapolis to prove that they are still a competent football team that hasn’t forgotten how to win games. While it may be hard to believe, the Colts’ offense and defense may not look totally hopeless against the Dolphins this week. 5 bold predictions for the Indianapolis Colts Week 10 matchup with the Dolphins 1. Jonathan Taylor finally rushes for over 100 yards Shockingly, an entire year has passed since star running back Jonathan Taylor last crossed 100 rushing yards in a game. Of course, the issue isn’t a lack of talent, but the dysfunctional state of the entire Indianapolis offense. Even Taylor isn’t immune to that. This season, Taylor has run for over 90 yards five times, before just falling short of the elusive 100-yard mark. Against Miami, the conditions could be perfect for a big performance from Taylor. The Colts shouldn’t be playing from behind and can lean on him all game. A full workload against a mediocre defense is exactly what Taylor needs to break his 16-game curse. 2. Tyler Warren bounces back The Indianapolis wide receiver room has been decimated. Alec Pierce is still on Injured Reserve , while Josh Downs and Keenan Allen were traded on deadline day earlier this week. Those were the Colts’ top three wideouts entering the season, and none of them will be on the field in Week 10. Someone has to step up and fill the void. It’s been a quiet season for tight end Tyler Warren, who hasn’t been able to keep up his rookie-year momentum. Given the lack of proven pass-catching options in Indianapolis, Warren is poised to have a bounce-back game against the Dolphins. The Colts will likely target him early and often this week. Expect Warren to embrace his newly expanded role. 3. Indianapolis pass rush dominates After struggling for most of this season, the Colts’ pass rush has looked better recently with back-to-back-to-back three-sack games. Young playmakers Adetomiwa Adebawore, Laiatu Latu, and JT Tuimoloau have all stepped up. Now, the unit faces a team that has already allowed 21 sacks through seven games. On top of that, hyper-mobile Miami QB Malik Willis will miss the game due to injury, meaning second-year pro Kyle McCord is slated to make his NFL debut. McCord doesn’t have Willis-level speed to escape the pocket. He has also never played a regular season snap, so this will be his first time facing an NFL-level pass rush. Indianapolis’ recent success generating pressure, combined with Miami’s unfortunate QB situation, sets the stage for the Colts’ first 4+ sack performance of 2026. 4. Ollie Gordon has the best game of his career Indianapolis has the third-worst run defense in the league, allowing 137 rushing yards per game. Now, they face Miami running back Ollie Gordon, who has impressed in his second NFL season after taking over for the injured De’Von Achane. Gordon ran for a career-high 103 yards back in Week 7, but has a chance to set a new personal record against the Colts. Multiple running backs have had monster stat lines against Indianapolis this season, including Derrick Henry, Kenneth Walker III, Jaylen Warren, Bhayshul Tuten, and Javonte Williams. Gordon could easily join that group this week. 5. Colts end their five-game losing streak For the last five weeks, Indianapolis has been in a downward spiral with seemingly no end in sight. The losses are piling up and, after a series of trades, the Colts are now playing with a skeleton crew. It’s hard to imagine this group racking up many more wins before the end of the year. That being said, Week 10 will be Indianapolis’ best shot at victory in a long time. The Dolphins have only won once all year and are starting a backup QB this week. There is no such thing as an easy win for this version of the Colts, but a matchup against Miami and McCord is the closest thing to it. Indianapolis should be able to break their losing streak and hopefully breathe new life into their season. away.blurb: Bleacher Report • 3h Jameis Yells 'Who Let the Dogs Out' 🐶 Bleacher Report • 14h Steph Out 2+ Weeks with Oblique Tear The Miami Dolphins will be without starting quarterback Malik Willis for at least a month. Willis was placed on injured reserved on Tuesday, with The Ringer's Tom Pelissero reporting that Willis has been battling a groin injury that developed into a core muscle injury. The injury is not considered season-ending, but he will miss at least the next four weeks. Second-year quarterback Kyle McCord will make his first career start on Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts. Willis started all eight games for the 1-7 Dolphins and threw for 1,396 yards, six touchdowns and six interceptions. He was also Miami's second-leading rusher with 238 yards and three more scores on the ground. McCord will be taking over a Dolphins offense that ranks 31st in the NFL with 15.8 points per game. The 2025 sixth-round pick was traded to Miami in August after spending the preseason with the Green Bay Packers. In his final collegiate season in 2024, he threw for 4,779 yards, 34 touchdowns and 12 interceptions while leading Syracuse to a 10-3 record. In addition to losing Willis to IR, the Dolphins suffered a major blow to their defense after standout defensive tackle Zach Sieler suffered a season-ending ruptured biceps. The 31-year-old team captain is one of the veteran leaders on a rebuilding team, and his presence on the field will surely be missed. away.headline: Panthers injury report is full of reinforcements
away.blurb: Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks The Carolina Panthers are flailing as they try to stay afloat at the top of the ever pitiful NFC South. The team has dropped three straight games with a skeleton crew of a secondary and a revolving door of players on the offensive line. The first injury report of Week 10 brings good news though. It looks like a lot of key players are soon to return. The highlight of this injury report is all of the full participation from guys that have been out for extended periods of time. Mike Jackson, Jonathon Brooks, and Xavier Legette all had their practice windows opened on Wednesday. That doesn't guarantee that they'll be active on Sunday, but it does mean they need to be activated within the next three weeks. And the fact that they all practiced in full would suggest they're all very close to getting back to live game action. The Saints are very banged up along their offensive line. Starting center Erik McCoy is out. Both starters to his left and the backup left tackle are all dealing with their own injuries, though it doesn't seem like any will miss the game this weekend. Running back Travis Etienne is back at practice, but I wouldn't be surprised if he misses the game even after a limited practice since teams tend to be very cautious with muscle injuries like that. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images MacGregor Wells · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 1:42 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Jets lost their fourth straight game and seventh of their last eight on Sunday. The Jets are now 2-7 on the season. All playoff hopes have evaporated. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-21 record. We are reaching Kotite-ish levels of ineptitude. This week the Jets visited the Kansas City Chiefs. They kept it competitve for a half. In the first half the Jets outgained the Chiefs. They won the turnover battle. They had more than twice the time of possession as the Chiefs. They scored on four out of five possessions. The Chiefs scored only twice. And still the Jets trailed at halftime, 14 – 12. It was an ill omen. The second half was all Chiefs. They scored 21 unanswered points and cruised to a 35 – 12 blowout over the Jets. It was just one more humiliation in a decade filled with them. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-7 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. Now the Jets limp home to face the first place Buffalo Bills in East Rutherford, New Jersey next Sunday. The Bills have won three straight games and six of seven on the year. Josh Allen is playing like an MVP candidate, as usual. The Bills offense is humming, leading the NFL in points scored. The Bills defense has had some issues, but they held the Baltimore Ravens to 144 yards of offense and just 10 points last week. This will be a formidable challenge for a reeling Jets team just trying to stop the bleeding. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Unsurprisingly the oddsmakers think the Bills will easily handle the Jets. The current line has the Jets home underdogs by 8.5 points. The game has an over/under of 51.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +400 while the Bills are -520. Any given Sunday and all that jazz, but an upset here seems like a bridge too far for the Jets. Perhaps they can keep the game competitive for a while as they did against the Chiefs for a half. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Buffalo Bills (7-1) visit the New York Jets (2-7) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium, with the AFC East rivals heading in dramatically different directions. Buffalo sits three games clear of second-place New England atop the division while the Jets have lost four in a row and sit but a half-game out of the cellar in the AFC East. The Bills enter the week with the NFL’s highest-scoring offense at 32.0 points per game and lead the league with 386.4 yards per game, powered by Josh Allen and a rushing attack featuring James Cook III . The Jets, meanwhile, are averaging just 20.2 points per game which begs the question: Can Geno Smith and the Jets score enough to keep up with the Bills’ elite attack? Working in the Jets’ favor is that Buffalo has a short turnaround after grinding out a 23-6 road victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night. It was a far more physical game than the final score suggests. The Bills managed just three points on their first six possessions, and Allen threw an early interception, but his 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 44 seconds remaining in the first half gave Buffalo a 10-6 advantage. From there the Bills wore down Minnesota, holding the ball for an extraordinary 42:32 and running 79 offensive plays. Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards, including a five-yard fourth-quarter touchdown, while Allen finished 21-of-31 for 234 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Buffalo’s defense was even better, limiting Minnesota to 178 total yards and nine first downs while forcing three turnovers. The Jets return home after a 35-12 loss at Kansas City. Despite an early 6-0 lead, New York’s offensive woes were impossible to ignore. Smith and co. repeatedly stalled and had to settle for four Jason Sanders field goals. The Chiefs led just 14-12 at halftime before completely controlling the second half. New York finished with only 229 yards, went 2-for-12 on third down and failed to score a touchdown, while Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards and was sacked five times. Breece Hall returned from a five-game absence caused by a quadriceps injury and produced 87 yards from scrimmage, while rookie Omar Cooper Jr. led the Jets with eight catches for 58 yards. Recent history adds another challenge for New York. home.blurb: Drafted by the Atlanta Falcons in the fourth round of the 2020 NFL Draft out of Fresno State, Walker has played for four NFL teams over the course of his six seasons in the league. New York Jets Sign 29-Year-Old Player After Loss to Chiefs Unlock the latest Heavy on Jets news — direct to your inbox. The New York Jets fell to 2-7 on Sunday after suffering a 35-12 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. New York has now dropped four games in a row and has seemingly had a very busy Monday as it sets its sights on Week 10. The Jets agreed to trade six-year safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a 2028 sixth-round pick ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. Not long after that, they made another notable roster move. Jets Sign 29-Year-Old Linebacker According to Connor Long of Jets X-Factor , the Jets are signing 29-year-old linebacker Mykal Walker to their practice squad. The move comes with Kiko Mauigoa still on injured reserve and Trevin Wallace currently dealing with an injury after missing Sunday's game against Kansas City. Walker is quite familiar with the Jets organization, as he appeared in 14 games for the team last year, primarily playing special teams and serving in a rotational defensive role. However, after roster cuts, the Jets ultimately released him with an injury settlement. NEWS: The #Jets are signing LB Mykal Walker to their practice squad, a source tells me. Walker appeared in 14 games for New York last season, contributing on defense and special teams. He was released with an injury settlement after roster cuts. — Connor Long (@connor_long15) November 9, 2026 He spent his first three seasons with the Falcons, appearing in 49 games and making 20 starts. In 2023, he joined the Pittsburgh Steelers before moving to the Washington Commanders in 2024 and ultimately landing with the Jets in 2025. Walker saw most of his production in Atlanta, but he has also made an impact with three other NFL teams. Across 88 career games and 30 starts, he has totaled 272 tackles, 14 pass deflections, eight tackles for loss, four interceptions and one sack. Tight end Dalton Kincaid is the only skilled-position player on the injured list. He has an ankle injury and was limited in Buffalo's practice session. Seattle is coming off a quieter offensive performance against the Arizona Cardinals, but this matchup presents a chance for the Seahawks to get back on track in a big way. The Raiders have one of the worst defenses in the NFL, particularly when it comes to stopping the run. Meanwhile, rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza is preparing for his first NFL start against a Seattle defense that has been one of the toughest units in the league. I expect the Seahawks to take advantage of both matchups. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bold Prediction No. 4: Jadarian Price scores his first NFL touchdown Credit: Matt Kartozian-Imagn Images This could finally be the game when Jadarian Price gets into the end zone for the first time in his NFL career. It's been a challenging rookie season for the first-round pick, who has yet to find his footing in Seattle's backfield. However, this matchup could be exactly what he needs to change the trajectory of his season. The Raiders have struggled mightily against opposing running backs, and Price should have opportunities to make an impact. With Zach Charbonnet also back in the backfield, Seattle has more options to attack Las Vegas. It is expected Price will take advantage of his opportunities and finally get that first NFL touchdown. Bold Prediction No. 3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba records 10+ catches, 125+ yards, and at least one TD Even though Seattle should have plenty of success running the football, that doesn't mean Jaxon Smith-Njigba won't have a monster afternoon. JSN is coming off a relatively quiet performance against the Cardinals, finishing with seven catches for 51 yards without a touchdown. That is not the kind of production we've grown accustomed to seeing from one of the NFL's best wide receivers. I expect a much different performance against Las Vegas. The Raiders have struggled to contain opposing offenses. I think he gets back to dominating opposing secondaries. Bold Prediction No. 2: Seahawks' rushing attack finally has a monster game The Raiders are allowing a league-leading 151.2 rushing yards per game. That's an invitation for Seattle to establish its ground game and take advantage of one of the NFL's worst run defenses. Seattle averages 110 yards on the ground. The Seahawks have yet to consistently get their rushing attack going, but this is the perfect opportunity to change that. With rookie Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back from injury, Seattle has the personnel to make life miserable for Las Vegas. It shouldn't matter who is getting the carries. I expect the Seahawks to pound the rock throughout the afternoon and finish with close to 200 rushing yards. And remember, I still expect Smith-Njigba to have a monster game through the air. Seattle could realistically finish with more than 450 total yards of offense if everything goes according to plan. Bold Prediction No. 1: Fernando Mendoza has a nightmare game in his first NFL start Welcome to the NFL, Fernando Mendoza . The rookie quarterback is getting his first opportunity to lead the Raiders after the organization made a major change at the position. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings . Unfortunately, his first start comes against a Seahawks defense that can make life extremely difficult for opposing quarterbacks. Mendoza does have some talented tight ends to work with, but Las Vegas' receiving corps is underwhelming. Seattle should be able to make things uncomfortable for the rookie, particularly if its pass rush can consistently generate pressure. It wouldn't be surprising if Mendoza throws a touchdown pass at some point. However, I expect the Raiders' offense to struggle for most of the afternoon. The prediction is that Mendoza finishes with fewer than 175 passing yards and completes less than 65% of his attempts. His first NFL start will be a difficult learning experience, and Seattle's defense will be the biggest reason why. picks.headline: Seahawks vs. Raiders Week 10 tracker: Injury updates, prediction, storylines and more
picks.blurb: Seahawks vs. Raiders Week 10 tracker: Injury updates, prediction, storylines and more - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search News Finance More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Scores / Schedules Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald is seen before a game | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Lee Vowell · 12th Man Rising Thu, November 12, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads About our Ads The Seattle Seahawks are 5-4 and head to Las Vegas to play the 4-5 Raiders at Allegiant Stadium in Week 10. Seattle will be playing with a backup quarterback, Drew Lock, and Las Vegas will have a rookie quarterback, Fernando Mendoza, in his first career start. Head coach Mike Macdonald's team still has the better roster, and should be expected to win, but the Raiders are better this season than in quite some time. A victory against Seattle would be huge for their collective confidence. Health could be a factor. Seattle's injury report was fairly lengthy, so even some players who perform in Week 10 might not be close to 100 percent. At least, the bye week follows in Week 11. Seattle Seahawks injury updates for Week 10 Anthony Bradford Charles Cross Ribs and quad Elbow and oblique Quenton Nelson Uchenna Nwosu Patrick O'Connell Connor O'Toole Personal matter Rashid Shaheed Jaxon Smith-Njigba Leonard Williams Sam Darnold has already been ruled out, so he won't play. Drew Lock was expected to be limited all week, but is expected to play in Week 10. Leonard Williams is already trending toward missing another game. He will be missed. Seattle will announce its full list of inactives an hour and a half before kickoff, and this article will be updated with the latest information. Raiders inactives and injury updates Thomas Booker Foley Fatukasi Shoulder and back Trey Zuhn III The Raiders are fairly healthy, but what doesn't show on their injury report is the trade of quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings. This means rookie Fernando Mendoza will start for the first time in the NFL. As with Seattle, Vegas will announce its inactives an hour and a half before kickoff. How to watch Seahawks vs. Raiders in Week 10 Date: Sunday, November 15 Time: 1:05 p.m. PT TV Network: CBS (KIRO 7 in Seattle) Announcers: Ian Eagle (play-by-play), Ross Tucker (analysis), and Evan Washburn (sideline reporter) In the Seattle area, you can also stream the game on NFL+, while nationally, you might need a subscription to YouTube TV's NFL Sunday Ticket to stream or watch the game. You can listen to the game on the Seahawks Mobile App, SiriusXM channels 123 or 269, Seattle Sports 710 AM, and KIRO Newsradio 97.3. Steve Raible will provide the play-by-play for the Seahawks broadcast, while Dave Wyman will do the analysis, and Jen Mueller will report from the sidelines. Storylines to watch for Seahawks in Week 10 How will Fernando Mendoza do? Obviously, what most national fans will be interested in is how well the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft will do in his first career start . While Vegas trading Kirk Cousins made sense, Mendoza's first two starts couldn't come against tougher defenses: The Seahawks and then the Denver Broncos. Presumably, head coach Klint Kubiak isn't going to let Mendoza throw the ball 50 times, but he could have a somewhat conservative game plan to operate with. Kubiak is a good coach, so fans should expect a difficult challenge, even against a rookie quarterback. Will Drew Lock succeed against a non-Arizona Cardinals team? The difference between Lock games and Sam Darnold games has been significant this season. Lock has turned the ball over in three games. Darnold has nine interceptions in six games. What fans have seen from Lock might not be reality, though. He played the majority of reps in Week 1 against the New England Patriots, but Week 1s are often lies. His other two games have been against the terrible Cardinals. Darnold has faced far tougher competition. Lock's true first test might come against the Raiders, who are eighth in the league with seven interceptions. Can the Seahawks succeed running the ball? Week 9 against the Cardinals looked quite a bit different offensively for Seattle. That is partly because running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price were healthier. To win with Lock, and even when Darnold returns, the running game needs to continue being good. The Raiders are tight for last in the NFL at allowing 5.0 yards per carry. They are also last in yards allowed per rushing attempt at 151.2. The Seahawks must run the ball effectively to win. Prediction for Week 10 Seahawks 21, Raiders 14 This game is difficult to predict due to a number of factors, including how good Mendoza might be and the overall health of the Seahawks' defense. If Leonard Williams and Uchenna Nwosu miss the game again, the normally lofty standard of Mike Macdonald's defense could be exposed by a good offensive coach for Las Vegas. The hope is that Seattle wins a fairly ugly game, one that will probably be close until the end. Hopefully, Drew Lock just plays another clean game. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Seattle Seahawks (5-4) head to Las Vegas on Sunday trying to establish some momentum in a tightly packed NFC West race, while the Raiders (4-5) are looking to rebound from one of their sloppiest performances of the season AND are looking to do so with rookie Fernando Mendoza making his first start of his career. The matchup is a monster challenge for Mendoza: Seattle has leaned on a defense allowing just 18.0 points per game, tied for fourth-best in the league entering the week, while Las Vegas has surrendered 29.8 per game, ranking last. So you expect the Raiders would look to lean on Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr. to run the ball and take the pressure off their rookie signal-caller…but know that the Seahawks allow an average of 89.1 yards per game (151.2 for the Raiders). Quarterback is also a storyline for the Seahawks. Sam Darnold remains sidelined with a quad injury after also reportedly cracking a rib against Chicago, while Drew Lock came out of this past Sunday’s game dealing with an oblique issue after previously battling elbow tendinitis. Seattle comes in off a much-needed 17-3 victory over Arizona, a game it controlled despite playing without starting quarterback Darnold. Backup Lock completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown, while tight end AJ Barner supplied both Seattle touchdowns, catching one from Lock and running for another. Zach Charbonnet , recently returned from an ACL injury, gave the offense some balance with 77 yards on 16 carries, and the defense held Arizona to 216 total yards and no touchdowns. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught seven passes for 51 yards and became the first NFL receiver to reach 1,000 yards this season. Las Vegas, meanwhile, is trying to clean up the turnovers after a 38-17 loss at San Francisco dropped it below .500. The Raiders were actually within 21-10 at halftime, but Kirk Cousins was intercepted on the first play of the third quarter and Jaden Dugger returned it 35 yards for a touchdown, beginning a disastrous second half. Cousins finished 22-of-32 for 216 yards, one touchdown and three interceptions as Las Vegas committed five turnovers, managed only 240 total yards and 24 rushing yards, and possessed the ball for just 21:42. Brock Bowers was possibly the only bright spot, catching seven passes for 111 yards and a touchdown. Sunday’s game is also a reunion of two franchises with considerably more history than their present-day conference alignment suggests. The Raiders and Seahawks were AFC West rivals from 1977 through 2001, and the Raiders lead the overall series 30-26, including postseason games. They have met only periodically since Seattle moved to the NFC, with the last meeting producing one of the wildest games of the 2022 season: the Raiders won 40-34 in overtime in Seattle, powered by Josh Jacobs’ 229 rushing yards and two touchdowns. Fernando Mendoza takes over at quarterback for the Raiders (4-5) after the team traded Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, and he faces a Seahawks team (5-4) that has won two of its last three. The Seahawks hold the clearest advantage because their strengths meet the Raiders' weakest units. Seattle allows 244 total yards and 155 passing yards per game, both best in the NFL, according to ESPN team statistics through nine games. The Raiders rank last in points allowed (29.8), total yards allowed (385) and rushing yards allowed (151) per game. The Raiders' path runs through their offense and the turnovers their defense creates. They score 26.4 points per game (eighth) and throw for 260 yards per game (fifth), with tight end Brock Bowers (658 receiving yards) and running back Ashton Jeanty (42 catches) as the main targets. Lock has thrown no interceptions in three appearances this season, so Maxx Crosby, who leads the Raiders with four sacks, and the pass rush have to create the mistakes. Seahawks vs Raiders win probabilities The 45-point gap still leaves the Raiders a realistic route to an upset, since the Seahawks are one game ahead in the standings and are starting a backup quarterback behind a patched offensive line. How could Seahawks vs Raiders unfold? The game can swing on who sets the tempo, because Seattle's best results come from controlled drives and the Raiders' come from disruption. If Seattle scores first and keeps Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price on schedule, Lock can work short throws to Jaxon Smith-Njigba while Mendoza chases the score. The Seahawks' recent results show how much clean early downs help. They allowed no sacks in their wins in Weeks 7 and 9, and they allowed five, five and three in their losses in Weeks 5, 6 and 8. If the Raiders get pressure early, Crosby and the front can push Lock into longer downs with Quenton Nelson out and Charles Cross uncertain. A takeaway or sack-fumble would then give Mendoza short fields, and Bowers and Jeanty offer quick, high-percentage targets when Seattle's coverage closes the deeper routes. Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Darnold (quadriceps and ribs) is out and could return after Seattle's Week 11 bye. Lock was limited Wednesday with right elbow and oblique injuries and is expected to start, with Jalen Milroe behind him. Macdonald said Lock will not take all the reps or throws in practice this week. Nelson, a guard acquired from the Colts, is also out after a knee procedure and is considered week to week. Cross (ankle) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger) did not practice Wednesday, and Macdonald has not made a decision on either. Receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee) was a full participant, and linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) was limited. Smith-Njigba sat out Wednesday for rest. What is the latest on the Raiders? The Raiders named Mendoza their starter this week after trading Cousins to Minnesota for a 2027 third-round pick. Coach Klint Kubiak, who was Seattle's offensive coordinator last season, said Mendoza has prepared well and is ready to lead the offense. Defensive tackles Thomas Booker (ankle) and Folorunso Fatukasi (shoulder and back) and offensive lineman Trey Zuhn III (concussion) were limited Wednesday, and the Raiders listed only four players on their report. Cousins went 6 for 25 on throws of 20 or more air yards, and NFL.com listed throwing contested targets open downfield among Mendoza's best traits, which gives Kubiak's offense more shot plays to choose from. Can the Raiders stop Seattle's ground game? San Francisco ran for 190 yards on the Raiders last Sunday. Seattle rushed for 120 yards against Arizona, with Charbonnet gaining 77 yards on 16 carries and Price adding 24 rushing yards and 54 receiving yards. With Booker and Fatukasi limited, the interior of the Raiders' line is the area to watch. Can Seattle protect Lock without Nelson? Anthony Bradford, a guard limited with a knee injury, and the rest of the line must hold up if Cross cannot play. The Raiders have 19 team sacks, and a short, quick passing game suits a quarterback who cannot take a full week of throws. Who wins the turnover battle? The Raiders have 14 takeaways, fourth in the NFL, while Seattle has 14 giveaways and a turnover margin of minus one. Darnold threw all nine of Seattle's interceptions, and Lock has none. Las Vegas lost the ball five times at San Francisco, including a pick-six on the first play of the second half, so a first-time starter who protects the ball would change that picture. If Lock cannot play, Milroe is next in line. The Raiders' Friday report will show whether Booker, Fatukasi and Zuhn are on track, and Sunday's inactives complete the picture. home.headline: Seahawks-Raiders Wednesday injury report: Leonard Williams still out, Rashid Shaheed returns
home.blurb: Seahawks-Raiders Wednesday injury report: Leonard Williams still out, Rashid Shaheed returns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks Seattle released the first of the three weekly injury reports, which is headlined by the health of backup quarterback Drew Lock, who is battling a lingering elbow injury and a new oblique injury. Lock was limited in practice on Wednesday, with head coach Mike Macdonald indicating that the veteran is "making good progress" and may start against the Raiders. Whoever is under center will once again be working with a patchwork offensive line as stars Quenton Nelson and Charles Cross did not practice. Nelson is battling a knee injury that might hold him out for his second straight game while Cross has been out with an ankle injury since Week 7. Backup guard Anthony Bradford continues to be hampered by a knee injury and was limited on Wednesday. On the defensive side, Leonard Williams remains out with a stinger that he suffered against the Kansas City Chiefs, and edge rusher Derick Hall was limited with a new back injury. Both would be a massive loss for the Seahawks front that will hope to ruin Raiders' rookie Fernando Mendoza's debut. It wasn't all negative for the Seahawks' defense, though, as signs are trending positive for edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu, who was limited with the ankle injury that's held him out of the team's last two games. Jack Freeman · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 12:29 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Seattle Seahawks emerged victorious in an injury bowl against the Arizona Cardinals last week, and it appears they may have to do it again on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders. The ominous messaging leaves the entirety of Seattle on Jalen Milroe watch yet again as the second-year player is the only other healthy quarterback on the Seahawks' 53-man roster and would come in if Lock couldn't play. The Seahawks offense appears to have a weapon returning as wide receiver and kicker returner Rashid Shaheed was a full participant in practice. Shaheed has had a quiet 2026, but remains a key piece to unlocking the Seahawks' offense as the organization is hopeful he emerges as a second option beside Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Meanwhile, the Raiders report was considerably smaller, so it appears they'll be near full-go against their former AFC West rival. For the Seahawks, they will have two more days of practice before setting game designations, so here's to hoping that the report shrinks throughout the week.

In all likelihood, Seattle won't rush Cross back and will still trot out Josh Jones at LT in Sin City. It's a good sign for Cross to potentially return after the bye week if he's already taking some reps now. Other than Jaxon Smith-Njigba returning to practice after a rest day, all of Wednesday's practice participations were the same. That means limited participation for pretty much everyone except for Sam Darnold, Quenton Nelson, and Leonard Williams. take on the Arizona Cardinals (3-6) Sunday in Glendale. The Rams’ struggles are the result of injuries and consistently inconsistent play. That said, they take the field riding a three-game winning streak that has pushed them into a tie with Seatle for second in the NFC West. The Cardinals are last in the division as a result of losses two of the last three weeks. Los Angeles has climbed back into the playoff chase behind Matthew Stafford , who has thrown for 2,374 yards and 16 touchdowns. Arizona averages only 19.8 points per game while surrendering 28.3, but there is one significant reason the Rams won’t take the Cardinals lightly: Arizona already beat them 18-16 on Oct. 18 at SoFi Stadium. Los Angeles extended its winning streak to three last Sunday with a 20-13 road victory over the Washington Commanders. The Rams’ defense has been central to the turnaround, holding the Chargers to nine points and Washington to 13 in consecutive weeks, and Los Angeles enters Sunday allowing only 20.1 points and 312.9 yards per game. The major concern is what Stafford will have around him. Star receiver Puka Nacua , the team’s leading receiver with 715 yards, is out after suffering knee and toe injuries, while Davante Adams remains on injured reserve with a hamstring injury and tight end Terrance Ferguson is also sidelined. It is up to Head Coach Sean McVay and Stafford to keep the offense functioning even with several of its most important weapons sidelined. Arizona’s most recent outing was far less encouraging. The Cardinals followed up a thrilling and improbable 33-30 overtime win in Dallas with a 17-3 loss at Seattle. The Cardinals are now 3-6 and, remarkably, 0-3 at home, while an offense already struggling for consistency is undergoing a major change at quarterback. With Gardner Minshew placed on injured reserve, rookie Carson Beck is set to make his first appearance against the Rams, putting even more importance on running back Tyler Allgeier and tight end Trey McBride , who leads Arizona with 598 receiving yards and five touchdown catches. The recent history makes this matchup particularly interesting because as noted earlier, Arizona has already pulled off one of the season’s bigger divisional upsets. On Oct. 18, the Cardinals went into SoFi Stadium and beat the Rams 18-16 despite failing to score a touchdown, riding six field goals from Chad Ryland . Los Angeles took a 16-15 lead with 46 seconds remaining on a Stafford touchdown pass to Colby Parkinson , only for Arizona to drive back into field-goal range and win on Ryland’s 43-yarder as time expired. That result interrupted what had otherwise been a Rams-dominated stretch in the rivalry: Los Angeles beat Arizona 45-17 in December 2025 and 37-20 in January 2026, and the Rams lead the complete series 53-42-2, including a 2-0 postseason record. away.headline: Puka Nacua Injury Update, Latest News on Rams WR's Status and Return Timeline Amid Knee Issue
away.blurb: Ultimately, the Rams are not going to be nearly as dangerous with both Nacua and Adams out. After all, Los Angeles is three games behind the San Francisco 49ers in the NFC West at 5-4 and on the outside of the playoff picture looking in at this point. The Green Bay Packers have the final wild-card spot at 6-3 and will face the Rams in Week 12 while Nacua is still out. The Los Angeles Rams will be without wide receiver Puka Nacua for the foreseeable future. The NFC West team placed the playmaker on injured reserve because of his MCL injury. What's more, head coach Sean McVay said his expectation is Nacua will miss "extended time." This is a change in direction for the Rams, as McVay initially told reporters that even though the wide receiver was going to miss "a significant period of time," the plan was not to place him on IR due to "semantics with the roster." Losing Nacua is quite the blow for Los Angeles seeing how Davante Adams is already sidelined with a hamstring injury. Nacua's injury happened during Sunday's win over the Washington Commanders, although he still finished with a head-turning 14 receptions for 150 yards and one touchdown on 19 targets. Through seven games this season, he has 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns. With both of Matthew Stafford's top receivers sidelined, the Rams will likely rely on the combination of Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield and CJ Daniels at the position. Tight end Tyler Higbee will likely see plenty of targets as well, although even he missed practice Thursday because of an illness. Nacua is one of the best wide receivers in the league and someone Stafford routinely targets double-digit amounts of time per game. There will be more pressure on the rushing attack to carry the offense with the two top playmakers sidelined, and there is also little room for error in the NFC standings. With remaining games against the Packers, 49ers and Kansas City Chiefs, as well as two against the Seattle Seahawks, there is a real chance the Rams will miss the playoffs. And those chances are much higher with Nacua not on the field.

away.blurb: Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks "Obviously, there have been a lot of people in and out, [which] sometimes takes that major joy out of a win sometimes," said Stafford. "You're like, 'Man, we just won, but we lost Puka for a little bit of time,' or we lost 'Ferg.' Some of those things, you ride the roller coaster a little bit of an NFL season. Try to be just as stable as you possibly can and understand that those things are going to happen. That's part of it. Then I think, frankly, there are opportunities for us to play better a little bit as well. Have injuries taken away from Rams' current 3-game winning streak? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Have injuries taken away from Rams' current 3-game winning streak? Brock Vierra, Rams Wire · Rams Wire Fri, November 13, 2026 at 12:30 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The recent narratives surrounding the Los Angeles Rams have been grim, despite the fact that the team is in the midst of a three-game winning streak. The issue that has kept the fan base from feeling happy is the plethora of injuries. Even though the team finally got Myles Garrett back, the Rams are entering the week unsure of who will be on the field against the Arizona Cardinals , as their injury report is littered with superstars. On top of Trent McDuffie, Kam Curl and Terrance Ferguson all being banged up to different degrees, Davante Adams, Kobie Turner, Jordan Whittington, and others have had to go on injured reserve, while Poona Ford and Jaylen Watson have been lost for the season. Due to all the bad injury news, quarterback Matthew Stafford was asked if it feels like the team is on a winning streak. Stafford spoke to the vibes of the team, the effect the injuries have had on morale, and how a unified focus on winning helps Los Angeles get through times like these. "Listen, the end game is to win the football game. We've done that three weeks in a row, looking to try and do that four times. The rest, to be honest with you, doesn't really matter because we scored a bunch of points in certain games and didn't win or held the other team's offense to very few points and didn't win. The name of the game is winning the football game. We're going to have to play as a team as good, if not better, than we have all season, and I'm looking forward to that challenge." The Rams travel to take on the Arizona Cardinals this Sunday, a team that beat them 18-16 in Week 6, which was Los Angeles' most recent defeat. Following this weekend's game, the team will have its bye before taking on the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve. The Rams hope some of their injured players will be ready to go after the Thanksgiving holiday. home.headline: Cardinals QB situation takes stunning turn with Gardner Minshew update: report
home.blurb: Following their 17-3 road loss Sunday to the Seattle Seahawks, the Arizona Cardinals received a major update on quarterback Gardner Minshew, who may have suffered a season-ending injury. On Monday evening, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.” Rapoport said Minshew suffered the injury before halftime but continued playing through it. According to Rapoport, Minshew will get additional testing done, but the injury could end his season and require a lengthy rehabilitation process. Minshew suffered the injury when he was hit by Seahawks pass rusher Dante Fowler while attempting a pass on the final play of the first half. The Cardinals quarterback grabbed his right arm after the rough hit, but continued to play. In Sunday’s game, Minshew completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and was sacked three times by the Seahawks defense. Seattle held Arizona to just 198 total yards of offense for the game. More news: Chiefs HC Andy Reid Reveals Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Ahead of Falcons Game The devastating update arrived days after the team traded veteran starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona’s unfortunate situation with Minshew has led to several developments, including Adam Schefter reporting that the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. This is Johnson’s 15th team in 14 seasons. According to ESPN , in an initial report on the Cardinals’ injury updates, rookie Carson Beck was expected to start on Sunday. The Cardinals drafted the former Miami Hurricanes quarterback at No. 65 in the 3rd round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Beck led his team to the College Football Playoff National Championship game, which they lost to Fernando Mendoza and the Indiana Hoosiers. The decision to draft Beck was met with mixed reviews, with many sports outlets giving the team a low grade for the pick. NFL.com’s Chad Reuter graded Arizona’s Day 2 picks, including Beck, an “A,” indicating he had “a lot of big-game experience.” However, Reuter also noted that Beck’s decision-making was too inconsistent to be a “surefire starter.” Beck appeared in the NFL Hall of Fame Game this preseason against the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 33-30 loss. With ESPN reporting that Beck is expected to start Sunday, he’s poised to take over for a 3-6 Arizona team, unless they opt to use Johnson instead. Unfortunately, both quarterbacks could face a challenging matchup for the team’s next NFL game. The Cardinals host a Los Angeles Rams team on Sunday, Nov. 15, that has now won three straight games to improve to 5-4 for the season. The Rams also just got back the NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, who recorded three sacks on Sunday in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders, so Beck or Johnson could face a difficult test for his first NFL start.
