picks.headline: 49ers vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 10
picks.blurb: 49ers vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Poch leaving for Man U Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Skubal suitors emerge 49ers vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 10 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 10, 2026 at 11:03 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads While the San Francisco 49ers made a fairly mild move, the Dallas Cowboys didn't move the needle at the trade deadline. But these teams meet in Week 10 of the NFL season, and here are bold predictions for the contest. Entering with a record of 7-1, the 49ers sit as the No. 1 in the NFC. Meanwhile, the Cowboys are trying to fight their way back into contention in the NFC East. They have a record of 4-5. The 49ers are road favorites, but only by 3.5 points. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) 49ers QB Brock Purdy will throw for 250 yards and two TD passes It's a matter of scheme that Purdy will have success , according to ESPN. "Kyle Shanahan will have answers for both the run and pass game Sunday in Dallas," Matt Bowen wrote. "Schemed throws for Brock Purdy that create open coverage voids off play-action, plus a multiple run game with Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black to attack a Cowboys defense, allowing 5.0 YPC (third most). I like the 49ers to cover on the road." Purdy has thrown for 1,980 yards this season with 17 touchdowns and five interceptions. He has been impressive and has the eye of head coach Kyle Shanahan, according to a post on X by 95.7 TheGame via Heavy.com. "Yeah, it's been amazing," Shanahan said. "Just since the first game he got in there. That's why I struggle at the beginning of the year when everyone's asking me, can I believe how good he's playing and how much better he's improved because he was so good off the bench versus Miami in his first game and the second week… taking us to the NFC Championship as a rookie. "And I think his second year took us to the Super Bowl maybe. So Brock's been the man since he's come in, and it's pretty unbelievable deal considering where he was drafted, how he started… very fortunate to have Brock." The Cowboys will have their hands full. Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb will get 8-plus catches and 90-plus yards The Cowboys are going to get the ball to Lamb. It's their best path to having a shot at beating the 49ers. Lamb left the win over the Colts with a sigh of relief, according to dallascowboys.com. "Those are the games that you love to end up on top," Lamb said. "We understand it was the same situation that we were kind of in last week, and we didn't end up on top then, so just finishing out the game, finishing out the drive — shout out to the defense for ending the game. "But I think I had, like, three penalties alone in the second half, and a fumble. Personally, I gotta take a real good look. The numbers look crazy, but it could have been more. And I'm always thinking about what could have been. So, as for me, as a leader on this offense,I feel like I've got to be better in some realms and just end the game." The 49ers are off to a great start. But before the season, the Cowboys were in the same conversation with them. Lamb said the Cowboys need to get the job done. "We know what we got going on, just the history of that [matchup], the guys that they have over there on defense and the prep, I mean, it's going to take a lot of a lot of preparation, and a lot of execution," Lamb said. "We can't have as many flags because they have a really good offense, too." Prescott will lean heavily on Lamb if George Pickens misses another game. But even if Pickens plays, Prescott won't forget who he needs to target, early and often. 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey will get in the end zone twice Look for McCaffrey to score on the ground and with a reception. The 49ers are going to get him the ball near the goal line. One thing that helps McCaffrey's overall usage is that Shanahan is more confident that he is ready to rock after a pre-bye injury slowed him somewhat, according to ninerswire.com. "No. I actually forgot about it," Shanahan said. "He had a good bye week, and he told me before the bye week in Christian style not to worry about it at all. He'll be fine, and he looked good all week." McCaffrey hasn't had a blowout game all season. His rushing high is 75 yards, and his receiving high is 61. But he has 10 total touchdowns, with nine of them coming off the ground. And consistency has been a hallmark. McCaffrey has scored in seven straight games. In three of those contests, he scored twice. The 49ers will need to be sharp offensively. Despite the way their defense has played, they will have trouble slowing down the Cowboys' high-octane offense. McCaffrey will likely need those scores to keep his team in good business. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton At one time…a few decades ago…the 49ers and the Cowboys was the top rivalry in the NFL. In 2026, Sunday’s game between the 49ers (7-1) and the Cowboys (4-5) features one team contending for a Super Bowl and the other simply battling to remain in contention in an underwhelming division. The contrast extends beyond the standings is explained in the numbers: the 49ers are averaging 29.4 points per game while allowing 19.5, compared with 27.3 scored and 26.2 allowed by the Cowboys. San Francisco arrives in Arlington following a convincing 38-17 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, a game the 49ers broke open with a turnover-fueled second half. Brock Purdy completed 17 of 25 passes for 232 yards and two touchdowns and also ran for a score, while Christian McCaffrey scored once on the ground and once through the air. San Francisco led 21-10 at halftime before Jaden Dugger returned an interception 35 yards for a touchdown on the Raiders’ first offensive play of the third quarter. That started a remarkable half in which the 49ers forced five turnovers. The Niners finished with 414 total yards, including 190 rushing, possessed the ball for more than 38 minutes. Dallas also enters the matchup following a victory, escaping Indianapolis with a 27-23 win over the Colts after trailing 23-20 with less than two minutes remaining. Dak Prescott immediately answered with a 46-yard completion to Ryan Flournoy , and Javonte Williams scored from one yard out with 1:08 remaining to put Dallas ahead for good. The Cowboys piled up 508 yards of offense to Indianapolis’ 271, with Prescott completing 21 of 34 passes for 335 yards and two touchdowns, CeeDee Lamb exploding for 10 catches and 195 yards and a score, and Williams rushing for 101 yards. But Dallas made life difficult for itself with two turnovers and 14 penalties for 153 yards. This is a rivalry that has produced some of the most memorable postseason games in NFL history, from “The Catch” in the 1981 NFC Championship Game to three consecutive NFC title-game meetings between the clubs following the 1992, 1993 and 1994 seasons. San Francisco currently owns the upper hand, leading the all-time series 21-19-1 and having won the past four meetings, including playoff victories of 23-17 after the 2021 season and 19-12 after the 2022 season. away.blurb: Porter missed Wednesday’s practice with an ankle injury. He was limited in practice last week and still couldn’t play against the Colts. The injury has bothered him since his Cowboys debut against the Texans on Oct. 4. He also struggled with ankle pain against the Cardinals, which limited his movement on the field. Ezeiruaku missed Wednesday’s practice with an ankle injury he suffered against the Colts on Nov. 8. He left the game and did not return, and the Cowboys later listed him as day-to-day. If he remains unavailable, Von Miller and Marist Liufau could see more playing time. However, he suffered another concussion in that game. As a result, he has been ruled out of the Week 10 game against the 49ers and could miss several more games. Mingo hurt his ankle in the win over the Colts. He tried to keep playing but couldn’t return, and he missed Wednesday’s practice as he recovers. Before the Nov. 8 game against the Colts, he was dealing with both hamstring and back problems and couldn’t play. He returned to practice on Wednesday, Nov. 11, but was limited because of his hamstring. His return to practice is a positive sign, but it’s still unclear whether he’ll be ready for the 49ers. Pickens practiced on Wednesday, but on a limited basis, the same status he had throughout last week. So, it’s not yet clear whether he’ll play against the 49ers. He has two more practices, on Thursday and Friday, before the Cowboys decide his status. “He tried to go. He wanted to play,” Brian Schottenheimer said, per ESPN’s Todd Archer. “He loves football. He returned to practice on Wednesday but was limited. Schoonmaker started having groin problems while preparing for the Nov. 1 game against the Cardinals. He missed two practices that week and was ruled out of the game. The injury limited his practice time again the following week ahead of the Colts game. However, he returned to full practice on Nov. 11. Bullard injured his calf in the Cowboys’ Sept. 27 game against the Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro. He left the game and did not return. home.headline: Cowboys Reportedly Sign New RB After 2026 NFL Trade Deadline, Tyler Goodson Injury
home.blurb: The TCU product was available because the New Orleans Saints released him after he appeared in six games for the NFC South team this season. He ran for 159 yards and two touchdowns on an ugly 2.8 yards per carry in those six games. Dallas Cowboys fans may have been hoping for a more consequential move ahead of Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET NFL trade deadline, but they reportedly did make a running back addition. Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News reported the Cowboys signed Kendre Miller to its practice squad with Tyler Goodson dealing with a knee injury he suffered in Sunday's win over the Indianapolis Colts. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters Monday that Goodson will miss "multiple weeks" with the setback. The timing was less than ideal for Goodson, as he was just starting to establish himself in the running back rotation behind Javonte Williams. He finished with a season-high 12 carries for 77 yards in the win over the Colts, which marked his second time in a three-game span with double-digit carries. Yet his injury put the team in scramble mode as it attempted to find another backup for Williams. Enter Miller, whom ESPN's Todd Archer reported visited with the Cowboys on Tuesday before their decision to sign him. Miller was also an occasional threat in the Saints' passing game with nine catches on a career-high 13 targets this season. While he isn't someone who is going to carry the offense on his back, the Cowboys won't ask him to do so. Instead, he will surely be put in a role where he is expected to fill in for Williams on a handful of series throughout games to keep the starter fresher for the stretch run. Next up for Dallas is a home game against the San Francisco 49ers.

home.headline: Cowboys Hit With Massive Injury Crisis as 16 Players Land on Injury Report Ahead of 49ers Clash
home.blurb: Porter missed Wednesday’s practice with an ankle injury. He was limited in practice last week and still couldn’t play against the Colts. The injury has bothered him since his Cowboys debut against the Texans on Oct. 4. He also struggled with ankle pain against the Cardinals, which limited his movement on the field. Ezeiruaku missed Wednesday’s practice with an ankle injury he suffered against the Colts on Nov. 8. He left the game and did not return, and the Cowboys later listed him as day-to-day. If he remains unavailable, Von Miller and Marist Liufau could see more playing time. However, he suffered another concussion in that game. As a result, he has been ruled out of the Week 10 game against the 49ers and could miss several more games. Mingo hurt his ankle in the win over the Colts. He tried to keep playing but couldn’t return, and he missed Wednesday’s practice as he recovers. Before the Nov. 8 game against the Colts, he was dealing with both hamstring and back problems and couldn’t play. He returned to practice on Wednesday, Nov. 11, but was limited because of his hamstring. His return to practice is a positive sign, but it’s still unclear whether he’ll be ready for the 49ers. Pickens practiced on Wednesday, but on a limited basis, the same status he had throughout last week. So, it’s not yet clear whether he’ll play against the 49ers. He has two more practices, on Thursday and Friday, before the Cowboys decide his status. “He tried to go. He wanted to play,” Brian Schottenheimer said, per ESPN’s Todd Archer. “He loves football. He tried to play and unfortunately just ran out of time.” Turpin injured the cartilage around his ribs in the Cowboys’ Oct. 18 game against the Packers. He went to the locker room, and the team initially listed him as questionable to return before ruling him out for the rest of the game. The injury kept him out of the game against the Colts. He returned to practice on Wednesday but was limited. Schoonmaker started having groin problems while preparing for the Nov. 1 game against the Cardinals. He missed two practices that week and was ruled out of the game. The injury limited his practice time again the following week ahead of the Colts game. However, he returned to full practice on Nov. 11. Bullard injured his calf in the Cowboys’ Sept. 27 game against the Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro. He left the game and did not return. Now it’s a waiting game to see how many of them return before Sunday’s game against the 49ers. home.blurb: Brian Schottenheimer told reporters, including Joseph Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News , that George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr., along with two other key players, are set to return to practice prior to Week 10. Dak Prescott could really use Pickens back in the lineup. With Jake Ferguson hurt, the Cowboys' passing offense is funneling through CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy. Pickens' return would open things up for everyone involved. Dallas won't be out of the playoff hunt if they lose in Week 10, but a victory would have them in great shape to make a second-half run to the playoffs. Getting Pickens, Porter, Overshown, and Turpin back would be a huge help. picks.headline: Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final
picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Poch leaving for Man U Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Skubal suitors emerge Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final (Sam Greene/The Enquirer / USA TODAY) Keegan Nickoson · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 11, 2026 at 11:53 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Joe Burrow accounts for four touchdowns for the fifth straight game Burrow is on a heater, scoring four or more touchdowns, whether throwing or running, in four straight games. In his last four games against the Steelers, Burrow has thrown 11 touchdowns and four interceptions, topping 275 yards in all four games. Interestingly, Pittsburgh is a great matchup for Burrow. The Steelers play zone coverage on 84.3% of dropbacks, according to Next Gen Stats, and Burrow is the best quarterback in the NFL against zone by completion percentage, at 74.7%. Jaylen Warren rushes for 120-plus yards Warren has become one of the league's most productive running backs this season, ranking sixth in rushing yards and first in yards per carry, at 5.9. Earlier this season against the Bengals , Warren ran for the second-most yards of his season, with 127. Two weeks ago against Cleveland, Warren topped that number with 143 yards. It was the first time all season he rushed for 100 yards in back-to-back games. The Bengals' defense has been inconsistent this season, struggling with tackling some weeks and shutting down opposing offenses and forcing takeaways in others. I think that, coming off a bye, the Steelers catch the Bengals on their back foot and feed Warren, who will have a big game. Steelers win 34-31 History is not on the Bengals' side in this matchup. After playing an overseas game, teams are 0-5 when their next game comes against a team coming off a bye. The Steelers are rested, while the Bengals are recovering from nearly a full week in Madrid. A lot is at stake in this game, with the winner taking sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Pittsburgh doesn't have much momentum, especially on offense, as its best wide receiver, DK Metcalf, has been struggling with drops lately. He has just 378 receiving yards this season and has topped 100 yards just once, with a 115-yard day against Cleveland earlier this season. Metcalf had just one catch for 4 yards on six targets against the Browns. The Steelers hit a snag at the right time, giving themselves a week to figure things out. I think the Steelers pick up a big win, halting the Bengals' momentum and getting a massive tiebreaker. Pittsburgh has done a relatively good job of keeping a cap on Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins over the last couple of seasons. Outside of Chase's massive 16-catch, 161-yard game with Joe Flacco at quarterback last season, neither has topped 100 yards in their last four meetings.

The former Steelers head coach knows exactly what this rivalry means after spending 19 years in Pittsburgh before stepping away from the role. He will now get to watch his old team from the NBC crew as the two sides prepare to meet on Sunday Night Football. Both teams enter the contest with 6-2 records and four consecutive victories, setting up a major meeting between two sides looking to strengthen their position in the AFC North. The Steelers' four-game winning run includes a commanding 27-6 victory over the Cleveland Browns in their most recent outing. Cincinnati have also found their rhythm, beating the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid. Burrow completed 82.8 per cent of his passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in that victory. However, the Bengals will have revenge on their minds after losing 30-27 to Pittsburgh during their earlier meeting this season. That defeat came during a difficult spell in which Cincinnati also suffered a second consecutive loss. Now, with both teams level at 6-2, the stakes are considerably higher. Tomlin will have a particularly interesting perspective from the NBC booth as he watches the Steelers take on a Bengals team that will be determined to settle the score on home turf. picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Steelers opening odds for massive Week 10 showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Poch leaving for Man U Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Skubal suitors emerge Bengals vs. Steelers opening odds for massive Week 10 showdown Alex Frank · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 12:05 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This is as big of a home game as it gets for the Cincinnati Bengals . It's mid-November, against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and first place in the AFC North is on the line. Both the Bengals and Steelers are 6-2 and have both won four straight games. Not to mention, these two teams have already played this season. It was in Week 3, with the Steelers winning 30-27 in Pittsburgh. Right now on FanDuel , the Bengals are 3.5-point favorites next Sunday night. The Bengals' moneyline is -200, while the Steelers' is at +168. The over/under is at 47.5. Sunday night could be an extremely physical game. It's an AFC North rivalry with sole possession of first place in the division at stake. Also, it's the Bengals and Steelers. That's all you need to know for the potential level of physicality. Pittsburgh stole the first game against the Bengals, aided by two Bengals turnovers in the fourth quarter that included Joe Burrow getting strip-sacked with the Bengals on the edge of field goal range in the final minute. The Bengals never ran an offensive play with the lead in that game, but there were some great performances from their star players. Joe Burrow was 28/37 for 282 yards and three touchdowns, Ja'Marr Chase caught nine passes for 98 yards and a touchdown, and Tee Higgins hauled in six passes for 90 yards and a touchdown. Mike Gesicki also caught a 25-yard touchdown on 4th&2 early in the fourth quarter. For the Steelers, Aaron Rodgers completed 19 of 34 passes for 292 yards and three touchdowns, while Jaylen Warren rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries. Eight different players caught a pass for the Steelers, with Darnell Washington leading the way with 67 receiving yards on three receptions. Roman Wilson, D.K. Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek each caught a touchdown for the Steelers. Rodgers currently has 1,871 passing yards and 13 touchdowns on the season, but he's also thrown six interceptions and is completing just 60.8 percent of his passes. Warren has 704 rushing yards and two touchdowns, while Washington and fellow tight end Pat Friermuth lead the Steelers with three and four touchdowns, respectively. T.J. Watt, as of Sunday night, leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks, and he also has nine tackles for loss. Cornerback Jamel Dean also has three forced fumbles. Bengals right tackle Amarius Mims held T.J. Watt off the stat sheet in that game, which bodes well going into Sunday night. The Bengals' offense scored on five of their eight drives in the first meeting in Week 3, gaining 352 yards of offense and rushing for 83 yards on 18 carries. Chase Brown rushed for 61 yards on 13 carries.

(Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images Frank Platko · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Updated Standings: Pittsburgh Steelers 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals 6-2 Cleveland Browns 5-4 Baltimore Ravens 4-5 Matchup: vs. Pittsburgh Steelers, 8:20pm EST The Bengals avoided a potential letdown game last week against the Atlanta Falcons in Spain, securing a 34-17 victory. After losing the first quarter by three points, the Bengals outscored the Falcons by 20 points for the remainder of the contest. Now riding a four-game win streak, having exceeded 30+ points in each game, the Bengals will return home for a primetime matchup with the Steelers. In Week 3, the Bengals suffered a 30-27 defeat against Pittsburgh and sit in second place now despite having the same record. Cincinnati's passing attack has been firing on all cylinders recently and Joe Burrow is hitting his stride. Over the last four games, Burrow has 16 touchdown passes while averaging over 300 passing yards. The Steelers are a Top 3 defense against the run but rank middle-of-the-pack defending the pass. The Bengals continue to struggle running the ball effectively, so they'll likely attack Pittsburgh's secondary regularly. Elsewhere, the Bengals' inconsistent run defense may be tested by Steelers' rushing attack that has totaled 148 yards and 200 yards on the ground in back-to-back games. The Bengals will need to slow down Jaylen Warren in the backfield, who has been a star this season. If the Bengals can make the Steelers one dimensional offensively, they become a much more beatable team. Matchup: vs. Cincinnati Bengals, 8:20pm EST Like their divisional counterpart, the Steelers have won their last four games to improve to 6-2, sitting atop the division by virtue of tiebreaker. Prior to last week's bye break, the Steelers defeated the Browns handedly by 21 points, their most lopsided win of the season and only their second win by more than one possession. Pittsburgh's momentum will be put to the test in a tough road environment this Sunday night with the AFC North lead on the line. The Steelers have won the turnover battle in three consecutive games. That will be an important factor for them to defeat the Bengals. Burrow has taken good care of the ball this year but did have a three-interception performance just two weeks ago. If the Steelers' defense can force a turnover or two and give their offense support with shorter fields, that will go a long way in helping them keep pace. On offense, the Steelers continue to long for better production from their pass-catchers to help unlock more downfield plays. Warren has been the team's only consistent playmaker and Rico Dowdle has ran well over the last two weeks in a complimentary role. However, D.K. Metcalf and company have been up-and-down in the passing game. In order to match Cincinnati's high-flying offensive attack, the Steelers will likely need to hit on a few explosive passing plays. Matchup: vs. Houston Texans, 1:00pm EST The Browns have now lost back-to-back games and are looking to get back on track before their upcoming bye week. In Week 9, they allowed a winnable game to slip through their grasp against the Saints, where they lost by one point in overtime. Shedeur Sanders impressed in his spot-start for Deshaun Watson at quarterback, but the Browns still struggled to run the ball and didn't start scoring much until the fourth quarter. Watson is set to return from injury to start this week versus his former team. The Texans have underwhelmed defensively this year but still have one of the league's more talented defenses, which will pose a challenge for the Browns — whose offense has struggled mightily at times this season. Houston has been vulnerable in pass coverage, allowing over 235 passing yards per game, leaving some hope that Watson can hit a downfield shot or two. The Browns will need to connect on some type of explosive plays or find a way to run the ball more effectively. Defensively, the Browns will need to bring their A game, as the Texans have prolific offensively at times in recent weeks. Last Sunday, they scored 44 points and C.J. Stroud threw five touchdown passes with nearly 400 passing yards. The Browns may be able to afford to sell out against the pass rather than the run, as the Texans rank even worse running the ball than they do. Matchup: vs. Los Angeles Chargers, 8:15pm EST The Ravens were thrashed by the Jacksonville Jaguars last Thursday night, losing by 20+ points for the third straight game. Baltimore's offense struggles hit a new low, as the team scored 10 points, gained 10 first downs and totaled just over 200 yards. With a hobbled third-string quarterback under center, the Ravens were no match for a talented Jaguars' squad. Fortunately, they will get the ultimate potential get-right matchup this coming Monday, taking on a winless Chargers team that is in disarray. Hopes for a potential offensive turnaround lie with new incoming quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who the Ravens traded for after Week 9. Brissett should provide a significant upgrade over Joe Fagnano as an experienced veteran who has proven, at the bare minimum, he can lead scoring drives and operate an offense at a competent level. Even with Brissett now under center, the Ravens need more consistency from their offensive line and breakthrough performances from veterans like Mark Andrews, Ronnie Stanley and Derrick Henry. Defensively, the Ravens have given up 30+ points in three straight weeks to three of the best offenses and quarterbacks in the NFL. They've played good halves and quarters, but the lows have been low. Coverage breakdowns and lack of impact pass rush continue to plague them. If there were ever a spot to have a convincing performance and force turnovers, this would be it. Chargers' quarterback Justin Herbert leads all quarterbacks in interceptions this season.

picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Bengals bold predictions for Week 10 Sunday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Poch leaving for Man U Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Skubal suitors emerge Steelers vs. Bengals bold predictions for Week 10 Sunday Night Football Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Wed, November 11, 2026 at 10:19 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The AFC North has been overshadowed by the NFC North to this point in the season, however this division is formidable and clearly the best in the AFC. There's probably just a small difference between this division and their NFC equivalents. The Pittsburgh Steelers and the Cincinnati Bengals are at the top of the division with 6-2 record, while the Browns are in third place with a 5-4 mark. The injury-plagued Baltimore Ravens are in fourth with a 4-5 record. The NFC North has three teams with six victories, while the first-place Chicago Bears have seven. The Steelers and Bengals are meeting Sunday night to determine the leader in the division. The Steelers have taken advantage of another memorable season from quarterback Aaron Rodgers . The 42-year-old announced that he would be retiring at the end of the season, and he has come through for head coach Mike McCarthy. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Rodgers has completed 175 of 288 passes for 1,871 yards with 13 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. He has always been known for his remarkable accuracy, and while he may no longer be at his peak, he is completing 60.8 percent of his passes. The years have slowed him down a bit when it comes to running out of the pocket, and that's something that Rodgers wants to avoid. The Bengals are surging as they prepare for this game against their division rivals. They have won four straight games after a 2-2 start and they are anxious to establish their explosive offense against the nasty Steelers defense. The Steelers defeated the Bengals 30-27 when the two teams met in Pittsburgh in Week 3. Dynamic QB Joe Burrow will throw for 250-plus yards and 3 TDs Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images There's little doubt that Joe Burrow is among the most gifted quarterback in recent memory. Burrow has been troubled by injuries in recent years, but he is healthy and has been showing off his remarkable skill level through the first half of the season. Burrow has completed a shocking 74.0 percent of his passes. He has connected on 219 of 296 passes for 2,386 yards with 23 TDs and 6 interceptions. He appears to be in the lead when it comes to the race for this season's Most Valuable Player award. Burrow has a remarkable 1-2 punch at the wide receiver position with Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase dominating opposing defensive backs. Higgins has caught 48 passes for 758 yards with 6 TDs, and he uses his speed and big-play ability to light up the scoreboard on a regular basis. Chase may be the best receiver in the NFL, although Jaxon Smith-Njigba of the Seattle Seahawks gives him a solid run for the title. Chase has 53 receptions for 647 yards and 7 TDs. Burrow will always look for Chase when the game is on the line. In addition to Higgin and Chase, tight end Mike Gesicki is an excellent red zone weapon, and he could be dangerous in this game. He has caught 26-252-6 through eight games. Rodgers will throw a pair of TD passes to his tight ends The Steelers don't have the superstars at the wide receiver position that the Bengals possess, but Rodgers has demonstrated that he doesn't need the same kind of big plays that the Bengals regularly produce. Wideout DK Metcalf is leading the Steelers in reception. He has caught 33 of 65 targets for 378 yards with 1 TD. More has been expected from Metcalf, and he needs to play more consistently in the second half of the season. The most productive receivers the Steelers have for red zone activity are tight ends Darnell Washington and Pat Freiermuth. Washington uses his size and strength to catch the ball in the end zone. He has 19 receptions for 254 yards and 3 TDs. Freiermuth has a bit more range than Washington, and he has caught 25-235-4. Running back Jaylen Warren has also demonstrated that he can catch passes out of the backfield in addition to his solid ground attack. Warren has caught 25-294-1, and he is also the team's leading rusher 704 yards, a 5.9 yards per carry average and 2 TDs. T.J. Watt will try to limit Burrow's production with 2.0 sacks If the Steelers are going to hold the Bengals' offensive production in check, it will almost certainly involve a powerful game from outside linebacker T.J. Watt. He leads the Bengals with 7.5 sacks and 9.5 tackles for loss. He also has 3 passes defensed, 1 interception that he returned for a touchdown, 1 forced fumble and 1 fumble recovery. Linebacker Payton Wilson is also a key contributor with a team-leading 69 tackles, 7 tackles for loss, 3 passes defensed, 1 interception and 1 fumble recovery. The Steelers rank 7th in total defense, as they are allowing 305.6 yards per game. They are even better as a scoring defense, ranking 4th and allowing just 18.0 points per game. If the Steelers are going to keep the Bengals in check and prevent Burrow from having a huge game, Watt & Co. will have to come up with a peak effort here. away.headline: Pittsburgh Steelers safety goes down with ankle injury
away.blurb: PITTSBURGH — Pittsburgh Steelers safety DeShon Elliott popped up on the team’s Wednesday injury report with an ankle injury, but he was limited in practice. Elliott has played a total of 28 snaps over the last two games since his return. That could be the Steelers easing him back into things, but it seems they trust the rookie in Spears-Jennings to assume many of the responsibilities next to Jaquan Brisker. Elliott, who returned three weeks ago from a knee injury he suffered last season, should still be able to play this week as long as he continues to practice for the Steelers. The ankle injury is not related to his knee. He has yet to regain his starting spot from rookie Robert Spears-Jennings, who has impressed the Steelers over his first eight games. Spears-Jennings has played over 45 percent of the snaps, while Elliott has come in during three safety sets and other sub-package personnel groupings. Pittsburgh will face the Cincinnati Bengals, who bring a high-powered attack to the table, in a game with Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins. The Steelers were able to knock off the Bengals at Acrisure Stadium 30-27 in Week 3 behind a huge performance from Jaylen Warren and the offense. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit pennlive.com. away.headline: Bengals face historic scheduling disadvantage against Steelers
away.blurb: The Bengals return to Paycor Stadium following a 34-17 victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid, but they'll face a Pittsburgh Steelers team that enjoyed a week to prepare. Local News Sports Opinion NKY Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals BENGALS Bengals face historic scheduling disadvantage against Steelers Shelby Dermer Cincinnati Enquirer Nov. 13, 2026, 12:30 a.m. ET The Cincinnati Bengals have a chance to take sole possession of first place in the AFC North, but history is not on their side. The Bengals have a favorable remaining schedule, which ranks as the 23rd-toughest in the NFL by opponent's winning percentage , and this primetime matchup against Pittsburgh is the Bengals' fourth and final game against an opponent that had a winning record last season. However, the Bengals are one of five NFL teams scheduled to play an international game this season, then play a team coming off a bye one week later. The Steelers had a Week 9 bye and have played just one road game since its last loss (Oct. 1 at Cleveland). This scheduling situation has happened five times before. The team coming off an international game is 0-5. The Steelers benefited from this spot in 2025. Pittsburgh was coming off its bye week last season and cruised to a 23-9 win over the Browns , which had lost to the Vikings in London the week prior. In Week 5 this season, the Eagles lost a heartbreaker at the buzzer to the Jaguars in London. They returned home for Week 6 and lost to the Carolina Panthers, who were coming off a bye, albeit Philadelphia was without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts. The Bengals are 0-2 all-time following an international game, though they had a bye week after visiting London in 2016 and 2019 .

away.blurb: Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks Courtesy of Wednesday's Week 10 injury report, the Steelers saw three players, who have missed time with their respective injuries, return to practice as full participants: wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf), cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring), and cornerback Doneiko Slaughter (hamstring). Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire · Steelers Wire Thu, November 12, 2026 at 3:58 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers received great injury news regarding three of their players ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengal s. Skowronek, who began his career with the Los Angeles Rams (2021–2023), also spent time with the Houston Texans (2024) before joining the Steelers in 2024. A solid wide receiver depth piece and special teams ace, Skowronek suffered his calf injury in Week 5 and has missed the past three games. Echols, who began his career with the New York Jets (2021–2024), joined the Steelers in 2025 free agency. An underrated contributor for Pittsburgh's defense last season, Echols suffered his hamstring injury during Week 6 and has missed the past two games. Slaughter, who began his NFL career with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2025), joined the Steelers on a reserve/future contract in January 2026. After a strong preseason and training camp, Slaughter was signed back to the active roster on October 10, but unfortunately suffered a hamstring injury in Week 7 and has missed the past game. The fact that Skowronek, Echols, and Slaughter were able to be full participants at Wednesday's practice gives them an excellent shot at returning in Week 10 for Sunday Night Football against the Bengals . home.headline: Bengals face historic scheduling disadvantage against Steelers
home.blurb: The Bengals return to Paycor Stadium following a 34-17 victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid, but they'll face a Pittsburgh Steelers team that enjoyed a week to prepare. Local News Sports Opinion NKY Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals BENGALS Bengals face historic scheduling disadvantage against Steelers Shelby Dermer Cincinnati Enquirer Nov. 13, 2026, 12:30 a.m. ET The Cincinnati Bengals have a chance to take sole possession of first place in the AFC North, but history is not on their side. The Bengals have a favorable remaining schedule, which ranks as the 23rd-toughest in the NFL by opponent's winning percentage , and this primetime matchup against Pittsburgh is the Bengals' fourth and final game against an opponent that had a winning record last season. However, the Bengals are one of five NFL teams scheduled to play an international game this season, then play a team coming off a bye one week later. The Steelers had a Week 9 bye and have played just one road game since its last loss (Oct. 1 at Cleveland). This scheduling situation has happened five times before. The team coming off an international game is 0-5. The Steelers benefited from this spot in 2025. Pittsburgh was coming off its bye week last season and cruised to a 23-9 win over the Browns , which had lost to the Vikings in London the week prior. In Week 5 this season, the Eagles lost a heartbreaker at the buzzer to the Jaguars in London. They returned home for Week 6 and lost to the Carolina Panthers, who were coming off a bye, albeit Philadelphia was without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts. The Bengals are 0-2 all-time following an international game, though they had a bye week after visiting London in 2016 and 2019 .

home.headline: Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals
home.blurb: Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks Courtesy of Wednesday's Week 10 injury report, the Steelers saw three players, who have missed time with their respective injuries, return to practice as full participants: wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf), cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring), and cornerback Doneiko Slaughter (hamstring). Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire · Steelers Wire Thu, November 12, 2026 at 3:58 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers received great injury news regarding three of their players ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengal s. Skowronek, who began his career with the Los Angeles Rams (2021–2023), also spent time with the Houston Texans (2024) before joining the Steelers in 2024. A solid wide receiver depth piece and special teams ace, Skowronek suffered his calf injury in Week 5 and has missed the past three games. Echols, who began his career with the New York Jets (2021–2024), joined the Steelers in 2025 free agency. An underrated contributor for Pittsburgh's defense last season, Echols suffered his hamstring injury during Week 6 and has missed the past two games. Slaughter, who began his NFL career with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2025), joined the Steelers on a reserve/future contract in January 2026. After a strong preseason and training camp, Slaughter was signed back to the active roster on October 10, but unfortunately suffered a hamstring injury in Week 7 and has missed the past game. The fact that Skowronek, Echols, and Slaughter were able to be full participants at Wednesday's practice gives them an excellent shot at returning in Week 10 for Sunday Night Football against the Bengals . Cornerback DJ Turner II (heel) was also limited. There was a chance he wouldn’t play last Sunday, but he was able to Stay in the field for nearly the entire game. Cincinnati will likely take it easy with him until his ankle is fully healed. Defense end Cedric Johnson is notably not included in the injury report, A great sign that his ankle/foot Injury from last week is no longer a concern. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) aggravated his quad injury during Week 7 and is still week-to-week. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen had his usual rest day. That's one way for the Chargers to take pressure off their offensive line, especially if Ladd McConkey is healthy enough to handle his usual workload. 4. Something's gotta give: Right? Los Angeles is 0-8, the NFL's only remaining winless team. Baltimore has dropped four in a row to plummet to the bottom of the AFC North after a 4-1 start. Someone will win in primetime. Unless there's a tie. 5. Home is for the birds: Baltimore is 2-11 ATS at home since the start of last season, failing to cover by 9.7 points per game, according to Evan Abram's NFL betting primer. The Ravens have failed to cover the spread in eight straight home games, which is the longest home against-the-spread skid in franchise history. 6. Primetime Herbert: With Justin Herbert, the Chargers are 18-8 ATS in primetime night games, winning six in a row outright since 2024. will make his Baltimore debut on Monday Night Football as Baltimore attempts to break its four-game losing streak with the winless Los Angeles Chargers (0-8). Los Angeles has lost its last three games by 22, 26, and 23 points. The Chargers have had three games decided by six, seven, and eight points, but none within the 4.5-point spread for Monday Night Football. Mike McDaniel ‘s offense failed to score a touchdown on 37-straight drives until last week in the fourth quarter against Houston (44-22 loss), but Los Angeles does have a positive matchup at Baltimore. The Ravens defense has given up 33, 36, and 35 points over the past three games, plus 27 total points in the first quarter. Baltimore’s defense is struggling with injuries, specifically in the secondary this week; Kyle Hamilton , Nate Wiggins , and Jaylinn Hawkins are all questionable. With all the attention on the upgrade at quarterback position, we can’t ignore the issues on the Ravens’ defense. We all have to admit, Brissett is a major upgrade over Joe Fagnano and newly signed third-stringer Kedon Slovis . However, the playbook will be limited, and the connection with the receivers won’t be immediate. I’d expect shorter passes and rhythm-builders for Brissett this week, but no matter what he does, it’ll be better than the 60 yards on 10-of-18 they got from Fagnano in last week’s 33-10 loss to the Jaguars. Quarterback matchup for Chargers vs Ravens · Baltimore : Jacoby Brissett — Brissett will make his Baltimore debut after playing in 22 games with the Arizona Cardinals, including eight starts this season. Brissett has 10 passing touchdowns to seven interceptions and has had five games with more than 200 passing yards and three with multi-touchdown tosses. The 33-year-old gives Baltimore veteran leadership and a chance to make the playoffs after a 4-5 start. With Arizona, Brissett ranked 25th and 26th in passer rating versus man and zone, 15th and 18th in completion percentage against man (59.2%) and zone (67.8%), plus 30th in deep ball completion percentage (19.4%), and 32nd in pressured completion percentage (41.5%). Not exactly game-breaker numbers, but more like game-manager, which is what Brissett is at this point in his career. · Los Angeles: Justin Herbert — No one expected Herbert’s season to go this poorly. After 23 touchdowns to three interceptions, then 26 touchdowns to six interceptions, Herbert has started the year with six touchdowns and 11 interceptions! He hasn’t thrown for two or more touchdowns in a game yet this season, and he’s still looking for his first 300-yard passing game, something he did three times last year. Herbert has been one of the worst quarterbacks in the league running play action. He has a 41.6% play-action completion percentage (34th) and 45.5% catchable pass rate (33rd). With the Chargers running the eighth-most play-action passes on passing plays, that is not ideal. Herbert also leads the league in danger throws (23) and has the second-most interceptable passes (16). At least he will be facing a banged-up secondary on Monday Night Football. The Ravens are 1-3 at home, so their 34-point edge in the market rests largely on the Chargers' 0-8 record and the Chargers' scoring problems. How could Chargers vs Ravens unfold? The Ravens can shorten the game by running. They gained 172 yards on the ground against Jacksonville last Thursday, including Justice Hill's 65-yard touchdown, but managed only 55 net passing yards with Joe Fagnano at quarterback. Brissett threw for 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions in eight starts for Arizona before the Cardinals benched him, according to Sportsnet, so offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has a more experienced passer to pair with Henry. The Chargers need to change the shape of the game. They went 12 straight quarters and 37 offensive drives without a touchdown before Quentin Johnston's 58-yard score against Houston, according to ESPN. Omarion Hampton leads the team with 369 rushing yards, and Herbert has completed 144 of 235 passes, but his 11 interceptions lead the NFL, tied with New England's Drake Maye. Minter spent the last two seasons running the Chargers' defense and knows their staff, including coordinator Chris O'Leary, whom he mentored. That familiarity gives the Ravens a detailed read on the opposition, and the offense he now faces, run by Mike McDaniel, has produced little against anyone this season. What is the latest team news? Both teams carry questions at quarterback and in the secondary, and the statuses can change before the final injury designations arrive. What is the latest on the Chargers? Herbert is listed as questionable with an injury to the middle finger of his left, non-throwing hand. X-rays were negative, and Harbaugh said Monday that he "should be good to go." Herbert left the Texans game in the fourth quarter, and DJ Uiagalelei finished it. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey is questionable after back spasms kept him out of the Texans game. Harbaugh described him as day-to-day on Monday, according to NDTV US Sports. Cornerbacks Isas Waxter and Cam Hart and defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe all hurt ankles against Houston, and Harbaugh said the Chargers would "see how the week goes." What is the latest on the Ravens? Minter said Monday that he expects Brissett to start. Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) are on injured reserve, and Fagnano, the undrafted rookie who started against Jacksonville, has dealt with an ankle issue. Safety Kyle Hamilton is questionable with a hip injury, and Minter said he "looks fairly good." Cornerback Nate Wiggins (illness) and safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) are also questionable, and Minter was optimistic about both returning this week. What could decide Chargers vs Ravens? Three matchups look most likely to separate two teams that have combined for one win in their last 10 games. Can the Chargers protect Herbert? The Chargers rank 31st of 32 teams in sacks allowed with 31, and Herbert went down a career-high eight times against Houston. The Ravens have 17 sacks in nine games, led by Mike Green with 3.5, but they had just two in their last three games after sacking Cleveland five times in Week 6. If the pass rush stays quiet, Herbert gets the time his offense has lacked. Can Brissett give the Ravens a different offense? The Ravens have had 11 days since their last game and the Chargers eight, which gives Brissett more time to learn Doyle's offense. Zay Flowers leads the team with 614 receiving yards, and the Chargers allow 27.4 points per game, tied for 28th. The Chargers' defense does rank eighth in opponent third-down rate at 34.3%, so Brissett cannot count on easy conversions. Who wins the turnover battle? The Chargers have 19 giveaways, tied for 31st, and a turnover margin of minus-seven. They turned the ball over at least twice in each of their last five games. The Ravens gave it away three times in each of their last two games, so a short field is the quickest way either offense can find points. What could move Chargers vs Ravens prediction? Herbert's final designation and McConkey's availability decide how much the Chargers can threaten a Ravens secondary that allowed 280 net passing yards to Buffalo and 242 to Jacksonville. On the Ravens side, Brissett's confirmation as the starter and the status of Hamilton, Wiggins and Hawkins shape both their passing game and their coverage. away.headline: Justin Herbert Injured, DJ Uiagalelei Makes NFL Debut as Chargers Fall to 0-8 in Loss to Texans
away.blurb: "Could be a fracture, we'll find out," Harbaugh told reporters after the game on Sunday. The Chargers quarterback, who went undrafted out of Florida State, came in for Herbert late in the fourth quarter as his team trailed big. The prospect of Uiagalelei taking the starting job from Herbert would have sounded like a joke coming into the season, but nothing is out of the realm of possibility amid an 0-8 start. Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert avoided a fractured finger after suffering an injury during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans, coach Jim Harbaugh revealed on Monday. Harbaugh said on Sunday that Herbert wanted to finish the game, but the coaching staff thought better of it. Herbert said he will do "whatever I can to make sure I'm 100 percent." While Harbaugh noted Herbert wanted to play through the injury, the coach opted to have DJ Uiagalelei—who made his NFL debut on Sunday—finish the game. Uiagalelei's first drive ended with a touchdown pass. Uiagalelei finished his first NFL game with 24 yards and a touchdown on 2-of-7 passing. It had been another rough day for Herbert before he exited, as he had just 193 yards, a touchdown and an interception. Herbert came into the game with 1,398 passing yards, five touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Before Sunday, he hadn't thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5. The Chargers' hopes of reaching the playoffs are essentially over at this point, but bringing in a new starting quarterback could give the team a spark heading into the second half of the season. Uiagalelei had a five-year college career with Clemson, Oregon State and Florida State, though he never quite lived up to the hype he had coming into college. After going undrafted in 2025, he signed with the Chargers but didn't make the 53-man roster. He spent last season on the team's practice squad. Over the offseason, he competed for the backup position behind Herbert but ultimately lost to Trey Lance and started the year on the practice squad. After Lance was placed on the injured reserve with a groin injury in September, Uiagalelei was promoted to the active roster, paving the way for him to serve as Herbert's backup.

away.headline: Chargers Final Injury Report Before NFL Trade Deadline
away.blurb: The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-7 and continue to shock the NFL world by showing an unwillingness to trade any of their players despite facing down a lost season in 2026. Los Angeles had hoped to right the ship and gain some momentum coming out of their week seven bye but looked listless against the Los Angeles Rams in week eight. game status for week 9 vs HOU DOUBTFUL — Kayode Awosika, David Njoku, Denzel Perryman, Brenen Thompson OUT — Deane Leonard, Kendall Williamson The Chargers do have other players who may be targets on the trade market but so far the word that has been put out to insiders around the NFL is that the Chargers are continuing to execute their plan of standing pat and trying to right the ship before heading into the 2027 season. The return of Donte Jackson to field is intriguing as he has been floated as a possible trade candidate and the Chargers have built up significant young depth both on the roster and the practice squad. Why Jim Harbaugh Called Out the NFL, Broncos After Failed Daiyan Henley Trade Chargers Final Injury Report Before NFL Trade Deadline Skip to main content SI.COM The Chargers have been battered by injuries this season. The joke around the NFL may be about the San Francisco 49ers electrical substation and its proximity to the practice facility but someone may need to look into the water in Los Angeles with the amount of injuries both LA teams have faced this season. By week six, the Chargers had over half of their original 53-man roster either on that week's injury report or on injured reserve. The Chargers are already down to their fifth option at left guard and despite hope for getting reinforcements to face the Houston Texans, it appears guard Kayode Awosika, who has not played since week two, is still at least one week away from returning to the field. The Chargers opened the practice windows for tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman this week but it appears that neither are ready to be activated off of injured reserve just yet. home.headline: Report: Lamar Jackson Informed Ravens Teammates Of Intent To Return In 2026
home.blurb: Report: Lamar Jackson Informed Ravens Teammates Of Intent To Return In 2026 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks Report: Lamar Jackson Informed Ravens Teammates Of Intent To Return In 2026 While it doesn't feel like there's much to be hopeful about as it pertains to the Charm City franchise, the face of it isn't ready to throw in the towel just yet. According to a report from NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , star quarterback Lamar Jackson told his teammates that he plans to return this season, with the hope of leading them on a late-season push for the postseason. After starting the season winning four of their first five games, the Ravens now sit at 4-5 and currently sit outside of the current playoff picture at the bottom of the AFC North division standings. With eight games and a bye week remaining on their schedule, in order to return to the postseason after just falling short last year, they'll need to start stacking some wins. The earliest Jackson is eligible to return is Week 14, when the Ravens host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, following the team's Week 13 bye. That will be five weeks post-op and at the earliest possible end of the spectrum for his potential return. If the Ravens can rattle off four straight wins or at least go 2-2 over that span, they'll be in a great position to make Jackson's push to return worthwhile. It'd be just in time for their final four games, all of which are against AFC North rivals, including a pair of bouts with the current division-leading Pittsburgh Steelers. If the Ravens want keep any glimmer of hope of still being alive and in contention for the postseason by the time Jackson is able to return to action, they can't afford to lose to the only winless team in the league. It might end up being a battle of backup quarterbacks if the Chargers decide to sit Herbert so he doesn't embarass himself or get further banged up in primetime.
